        // (v0.3-v18). Matching is now filename-based (see
        // parseRecordingFilename()/scanRecordingFolder()/
        // matchCallToFile()) — this tolerance applies to the name-based
        // tier only (comparing a name-prefixed file's own embedded
        // timestamp against the call's estimated end time). Locked value
        // from this session: 20 seconds — not 5, not the old 2 minutes.
        // v20 — UNCHANGED (explicitly not touched by this fix — see v20
        // changelog); the phone-number tier now has its OWN bound,
        // NUMBER_MATCH_MAX_GAP_MS below, and the two tiers now compete on
        // whichever candidate is actually closer rather than number
        // auto-winning whenever it qualifies at all.
        private const val FILE_MATCH_TOLERANCE_MS = 20_000L

        // v20 — REAL INCIDENT FIX: a number-tier candidate now only
        // QUALIFIES if its embedded filename timestamp is within this
        // window of the call's estimated end time — being the only file
        // for that number is no longer enough on its own (v19's flaw; see
        // v20 changelog for the real incident this caused). Deliberately
        // much looser than FILE_MATCH_TOLERANCE_MS (20 sec) — the number
        // already uniquely identifies the lead, so this only needs to
        // rule out "this file is from an entirely different day/session,"
        // not guard against cross-lead ambiguity. Locked value from this
        // session, confirmed with Srikanth: 10 minutes — generous for
        // realistic write/rename delays, nowhere close to the multi-day
        // gap that caused the incident.
        private const val NUMBER_MATCH_MAX_GAP_MS = 10L * 60 * 1000

        // v19 — a call whose match is still unresolved (no file found,
        // ambiguous, permission denied, not-answered, or a rejected/
        // failed upload) more than this many ms after its OWN call
        // timestamp stops blocking the watermark — see giveUpIfStale()
        // and syncRecordings(). Locked value from this session: 15 days.
        private const val WATERMARK_GIVEUP_MS = 15L * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000

        // v13 — non-http(s) URL schemes that shouldOverrideUrlLoading()
        // falls back to the Play Store for when no app is installed to
        // handle them. Only whatsapp: has a confirmed correct listing;
        // schemes with no entry here (tel:, mailto:, intent:, market:,
        // etc.) just fail silently on ActivityNotFoundException instead of
        // guessing at a store listing.
        private val schemeToPlayStoreApp = mapOf(
            "whatsapp" to "com.whatsapp"
        )
    }

    private val requiredPermissions: Array<String>
        get() = if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.TIRAMISU) {
            arrayOf(
                Manifest.permission.READ_CALL_LOG,
                Manifest.permission.READ_MEDIA_AUDIO,
                // v17 — FCM push wiring. Already declared in
                // AndroidManifest.xml since Build Order Step 5 but never
                // actually requested at runtime until now.
                Manifest.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS
            )
        } else {
            arrayOf(Manifest.permission.READ_CALL_LOG, Manifest.permission.READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE)
        }

    private val permissionLauncher =
        registerForActivityResult(ActivityResultContracts.RequestMultiplePermissions()) { results ->
            val allGranted = results.values.all { it }
            if (!allGranted) {
                Toast.makeText(
                    this,
                    "Some permissions were denied — the debug scan will show what fails.",
                    Toast.LENGTH_LONG
                ).show()
            }
        }

    override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
        super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)
        setContentView(R.layout.activity_main)

        webView = findViewById(R.id.webview)

        syncPrefs = AppPrefs.syncPrefs(this)
        securePrefs = AppPrefs.securePrefs(this)

        // v17 — FCM push wiring. Fetches the current token asynchronously
        // and caches it the same place FcmService.kt's onNewToken() writes
        // later refreshes to, so AndroidBridge.getFcmToken() always reads
        // from one converged source.
        FirebaseMessaging.getInstance().token.addOnCompleteListener { task ->
            if (task.isSuccessful) {
                val fcmToken = task.result
                syncPrefs.edit().putString(AppPrefs.KEY_FCM_TOKEN, fcmToken).apply()
                // v18 — sends this token to the server so send_fcm_push()
                // (cls_db.py) has something to deliver to. See this file's
                // v18 changelog note for why this reuses the existing
                // attendance registration route instead of a new endpoint.
                registerFcmTokenWithServer(fcmToken)
            } else {
                Log.w(LOG_TAG, "FCM token fetch failed", task.exception)
            }
        }

        setupWebView()

        // v15 — the native btn_sync ImageButton (and this click listener) is
        // REMOVED — sync is now triggered from the CRM web app itself via
        // AndroidBridge.syncRecordings() (see setupWebView() below), not a
        // floating native button. See this file's v15 changelog note.

        // v11 — hardware back button navigates WebView history first;
        // once there's nothing left to go back to, disable this callback
        // and re-dispatch so the system's normal default (close/minimize)
        // takes over.
        val backCallback = object : OnBackPressedCallback(true) {
            override fun handleOnBackPressed() {
                if (webView.canGoBack()) {
                    webView.goBack()
                } else {
                    isEnabled = false
                    onBackPressedDispatcher.onBackPressed()
                }
            }
        }
        this.onBackPressedDispatcher.addCallback(this, backCallback)

        requestPermissionsIfNeeded()
    }

    private fun setupWebView() {
        webView.settings.javaScriptEnabled = true
        webView.settings.domStorageEnabled = true
        // v13 — shouldOverrideUrlLoading override so non-http(s) links
        // (whatsapp:, tel:, mailto:, intent:, market:, etc.) are handed off
        // to the OS instead of the WebView trying to render them and
        // failing with net::ERR_UNKNOWN_URL_SCHEME. http/https requests
        // return false and load in the WebView exactly as before.
        webView.webViewClient = object : WebViewClient() {
            override fun shouldOverrideUrlLoading(view: WebView, request: WebResourceRequest): Boolean {
                val uri = request.url
                val scheme = uri.scheme?.lowercase(Locale.US)
                if (scheme == "http" || scheme == "https") {
                    return false
                }
                try {
                    startActivity(Intent(Intent.ACTION_VIEW, uri))
                } catch (e: ActivityNotFoundException) {
                    val playStorePackage = schemeToPlayStoreApp[scheme]
                    if (playStorePackage != null) {
                        try {
                            startActivity(
                                Intent(
                                    Intent.ACTION_VIEW,
                                    Uri.parse("https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=$playStorePackage")
                                )
                            )
                        } catch (e2: ActivityNotFoundException) {
                            // No Play Store app available either — nothing more we can do.
                        }
                    }
                }
                return true
            }
        }
        // v14 — bridges JS confirm()/alert()/prompt() to real native
        // AlertDialogs. Root cause of a real bug (Attendance Chunk B's
        // Weekoff/Leave Submit button silently doing nothing inside this
        // WebView while working fine in a normal desktop browser): with NO
        // webChromeClient set at all (the state before this version),
        // Android WebView's default behavior is that these calls return
        // immediately with no dialog shown — confirm() always resolves to
        // false — so `if (!confirm(...)) return;` in attendance.html's JS
        // was silently bailing out before ever reaching fetch(). Each
        // override below must call result.confirm()/result.cancel()
        // exactly once and return true; returning false (or never
        // resolving `result`) falls back to that same broken default
        // handling. Dismissing via the system back button or a tap outside
        // the dialog is wired to the same outcome as tapping Cancel
        // (confirm()/prompt()) or OK (alert() has no real "cancel" state).
        webView.webChromeClient = object : WebChromeClient() {
            override fun onJsAlert(
                view: WebView, url: String, message: String, result: JsResult
            ): Boolean {
                AlertDialog.Builder(this@MainActivity)
                    .setMessage(message)
                    .setPositiveButton("OK") { _, _ -> result.confirm() }
                    .setOnCancelListener { result.confirm() }
                    .setCancelable(true)
                    .show()
                return true
            }

            override fun onJsConfirm(
                view: WebView, url: String, message: String, result: JsResult
            ): Boolean {
                AlertDialog.Builder(this@MainActivity)
                    .setMessage(message)
                    .setPositiveButton("OK") { _, _ -> result.confirm() }
                    .setNegativeButton("Cancel") { _, _ -> result.cancel() }
                    .setOnCancelListener { result.cancel() }
                    .setCancelable(true)
                    .show()
                return true
            }

            // Not called by any CRM template today — implemented for
            // completeness/future-proofing per Srikanth's explicit request,
            // so a future feature using prompt() doesn't hit this same bug
            // a second time.
            override fun onJsPrompt(
                view: WebView, url: String, message: String, defaultValue: String?,
                result: JsPromptResult
            ): Boolean {
                val input = EditText(this@MainActivity)
                input.setText(defaultValue ?: "")
                AlertDialog.Builder(this@MainActivity)
                    .setMessage(message)
                    .setView(input)
                    .setPositiveButton("OK") { _, _ -> result.confirm(input.text.toString()) }
                    .setNegativeButton("Cancel") { _, _ -> result.cancel() }
                    .setOnCancelListener { result.cancel() }
                    .setCancelable(true)
                    .show()
                return true
            }
        }
        // v9 — JS bridge so the CRM web app itself (settings.html) can
        // trigger opening SettingsActivity natively. @JavascriptInterface
        // is reflection-based — ONLY annotated methods are ever reachable
        // from JS — so this anonymous object can never leak any native
        // capability beyond the small, deliberately-curated set annotated
        // below. Safe to trust with real native capabilities specifically
        // because webView only ever loads crm.asianbuild.in (no cleartext,
        // no user-navigable arbitrary URLs). v13 added a
        // shouldOverrideUrlLoading override above, but it only routes
        // non-http(s) schemes out to the OS — http(s) requests (including
        // this bridge's trusted crm.asianbuild.in origin) still load
        // in-WebView exactly as before, so this safety property is
        // unaffected — this bridge is reachable by the trusted CRM origin
        // only, never by arbitrary web content.
        //
        // v1 (APX Attendance, Build Order Step 5) — ADDED punchIn()/
        // punchOut(), launching the new PunchActivity with EXTRA_MODE set.
        // This object went from exactly one method to three; the "single-
        // method" framing in earlier versions of this comment no longer
        // described it accurately — corrected here. The safety property
        // that mattered (reflection-based exposure, only annotated methods
        // reachable) is unchanged and doesn't depend on the method count.
        //
        // The CRM's templates call these via:
        //   if (window.AndroidBridge) { AndroidBridge.openDeviceSyncSettings(); }
        //   if (window.AndroidBridge && typeof AndroidBridge.punchIn === 'function') { AndroidBridge.punchIn(); }
        //   if (window.AndroidBridge && typeof AndroidBridge.syncRecordings === 'function') { AndroidBridge.syncRecordings(); }
        // wrapped in that feature-detection check (the second/third forms
        // also guard against an OLDER installed APK whose AndroidBridge
        // object exists but predates punchIn/punchOut/syncRecordings — see
        // attendance.html v0.28's own note on why that fallback is expected,
        // not a bug) so the same button degrades gracefully in a normal
        // desktop/browser context.
        webView.addJavascriptInterface(object {
            @JavascriptInterface
            fun openDeviceSyncSettings() {
                // JS interface callbacks run on the WebView's own thread,
                // not the main UI thread — startActivity() must be posted
                // back to the main thread.
                runOnUiThread {
                    startActivity(Intent(this@MainActivity, SettingsActivity::class.java))
                }
            }

            // v15 — replaces the removed floating btn_sync ImageButton (see
            // this file's own v15 changelog note and activity_main.xml).
            // Same runOnUiThread{} pattern as openDeviceSyncSettings() above
            // — runSyncRecordings() itself does UI work (Toast, Snackbar),
            // so it must run on the main thread, not the WebView's JS
            // callback thread. No change to runSyncRecordings()/
            // syncRecordings()'s own logic — only how this is triggered.
            @JavascriptInterface
            fun syncRecordings() {
                runOnUiThread {
                    runSyncRecordings()
                }
            }

            @JavascriptInterface
            fun punchIn() {
                runOnUiThread {
                    val punchIntent = Intent(this@MainActivity, PunchActivity::class.java)
                    punchIntent.putExtra(PunchActivity.EXTRA_MODE, "in")
                    startActivity(punchIntent)
                }
            }

            @JavascriptInterface
            fun punchOut() {
                runOnUiThread {
                    val punchIntent = Intent(this@MainActivity, PunchActivity::class.java)
                    punchIntent.putExtra(PunchActivity.EXTRA_MODE, "out")
                    startActivity(punchIntent)
                }
            }

            // v17 — FCM push wiring. Returns the cached token synchronously
            // — safe with no runOnUiThread wrapper, unlike the methods
            // above, since this is just a prefs read, not UI work. The CRM
            // web app is responsible for actually POSTing this to the
            // server, using its own existing session auth.
            @JavascriptInterface
            fun getFcmToken(): String {
                return syncPrefs.getString(AppPrefs.KEY_FCM_TOKEN, "") ?: ""
            }
        }, "AndroidBridge")
        webView.loadUrl(crmUrl)
    }

    private fun requestPermissionsIfNeeded() {
        val missing = requiredPermissions.filter {
            ContextCompat.checkSelfPermission(this, it) != PackageManager.PERMISSION_GRANTED
        }
        if (missing.isNotEmpty()) {
            Toast.makeText(
                this,
                "This pilot needs call-log and audio-file access to test recording-folder visibility.",
                Toast.LENGTH_LONG
            ).show()
            permissionLauncher.launch(missing.toTypedArray())
        }
    }

    /**
     * v18 — POSTs a freshly-fetched/refreshed FCM token to
     * /api/attendance/register-fcm-token (the existing @token_required
     * route, unchanged server-side — see this file's v18 changelog note).
     * Same lifecycleScope.launch { withContext(Dispatchers.IO) { ... } }
     * off-main-thread pattern as reportCalls()/uploadRecording() below.
     * Silently skips (no error surfaced) if this device has no bearer
     * token saved yet — onCreate() calls this again on every future
     * launch, so it retries naturally once Settings' "Sync my token" has
     * been completed. Every failure path is caught and logged via Log.w,
     * never rethrown — must not crash or block app launch.
     */
    private fun registerFcmTokenWithServer(fcmToken: String) {
        lifecycleScope.launch {
            withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
                try {
                    val token = securePrefs.getString(AppPrefs.KEY_TOKEN, "") ?: ""
                    if (token.isBlank()) {
                        Log.d(LOG_TAG, "FCM token fetched but no bearer token saved yet — registration deferred to next launch.")
                        return@withContext
                    }
                    val bodyJson = JSONObject()
                    bodyJson.put("fcm_token", fcmToken)
                    val requestBody = bodyJson.toString().toRequestBody("application/json".toMediaType())
                    val request = Request.Builder()
                        .url("$BASE_URL/api/attendance/register-fcm-token")
                        .addHeader("Authorization", "Bearer $token")
                        .post(requestBody)
                        .build()
                    httpClient.newCall(request).execute().use { response ->
                        if (!response.isSuccessful) {
                            Log.w(LOG_TAG, "FCM token registration rejected by server: HTTP ${response.code}")
                        }
                    }
                } catch (e: Exception) {
                    Log.w(LOG_TAG, "FCM token registration failed", e)
                }
            }
        }
    }

    // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    // v0.3 — Phase B sync.
    // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    private data class CallEntry(
        val number: String,
        val timestampMs: Long,
        // "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss" — see v0.3 changelog note on why this is
        // NOT literal ISO 8601.
        val timestampStr: String,
        val durationSeconds: Int,
        val direction: String
    )

    private data class MatchedEntry(
        val leadId: String,
        val callTimestamp: String,
        val durationSeconds: Int
    )

    private data class ReportCallsResult(
        val recordingFolderPath: String?,
        val matched: List<MatchedEntry>
    )

    private data class RecordingFile(
        val displayName: String,
        val uri: Uri,
        val relativePath: String,
        val dateModifiedMs: Long,
        val dateAddedMs: Long,
        // v0.6 — MediaStore's own DURATION for this file, if it has one.
        // No longer a gate as of v19 (DURATION_MISMATCH_THRESHOLD removed
        // — see changelog); still logged as informational context.
        val durationMs: Long?,
        // v19 — the file's own embedded date/time parsed from its
        // filename (see parseRecordingFilename()) — now the PRIMARY
        // timestamp signal used for matching, replacing DATE_MODIFIED.
        // Null if the filename's date/time portion was unparseable.
        val embeddedTimestampMs: Long? = null
    )

    // v19 — parseRecordingFilename()'s classification of one candidate
    // file. isPhoneNumberPrefix distinguishes "+919494695877 2026-08-24
    // 15-00-55.m4a" (normalizedNumber set) from "Navila Mounika 2026-08-24
    // 17-18-10.m4a" (normalizedNumber null, only embeddedTimestampMs
    // matters). embeddedTimestampMs is null for either shape if the
    // trailing date/time portion failed to parse.
    private data class ParsedFilename(
        val isPhoneNumberPrefix: Boolean,
        val normalizedNumber: String?,
        val embeddedTimestampMs: Long?
    )

    // v19 — result of scanning the configured folder ONCE per sync run
    // (see scanRecordingFolder()). numberIndex and nameCandidates are the
    // two lookup structures matchCallToFile() consults for every call in
    // this run, so the folder is never re-queried per call.
    private data class FolderScanResult(
        val totalAudioFiles: Int,
        val candidatesInFolder: Int,
        val numberIndex: Map<String, List<RecordingFile>>,
        val nameCandidates: List<Pair<RecordingFile, Long>>
    )

    // v19 — outcome of matchCallToFile() for a single call. matchedBy is
    // a human-readable tag ("phone number" / "filename timestamp
    // (name-based)") logged alongside a successful upload. ambiguousNames
    // is only populated when two-or-more name-based candidates tied
    // within tolerance and neither was picked.
    // v20 — matchedGapMs is the winning candidate's own gap (ms) to the
    // call's estimated end time, for logging. otherTier/otherFile/
    // otherGapMs describe the OTHER tier's best candidate whenever one
    // existed but did not win (either it lost the closest-wins
    // competition, or — for the number tier — it existed but exceeded
    // NUMBER_MATCH_MAX_GAP_MS) — carried through purely so a future
    // incident like the one this version fixes is diagnosable from the
    // sync log alone, without a manual phone-side cross-check.
    private data class MatchOutcome(
        val file: RecordingFile?,
        val matchedBy: String?,
        val matchedGapMs: Long? = null,
        val ambiguous: Boolean,
        val ambiguousNames: List<String>,
        val otherTier: String? = null,
        val otherFile: RecordingFile? = null,
        val otherGapMs: Long? = null
    )

    /**
     * v19 — parses a recording filename of the shape
     * "<prefix> YYYY-MM-DD HH-MM-SS.<ext>" where <prefix> is either a
     * phone number (with or without a leading +91/+/91) or a name (saved
     * contact or TRAI CNAP network caller ID — both produce this same
     * shape, no need to distinguish them). Lenient about the extension —
     * .m4a/.mp3/.wav/.amr/.3gp are all plausible recorder outputs.
     * Returns null if the filename doesn't match this shape at all.
     */
    private fun parseRecordingFilename(displayName: String): ParsedFilename? {
        val dotIdx = displayName.lastIndexOf('.')
        if (dotIdx < 0) return null
        val ext = displayName.substring(dotIdx + 1).lowercase(Locale.US)
        if (ext !in setOf("m4a", "mp3", "wav", "amr", "3gp")) return null

        val base = displayName.substring(0, dotIdx).trim()
        val dateTimeRegex = Regex("""^(.+?)\s+(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}\s+\d{2}-\d{2}-\d{2})$""")
        val match = dateTimeRegex.matchEntire(base) ?: return null
        val prefix = match.groupValues[1].trim()
        if (prefix.isEmpty()) return null
        val dateTimeStr = match.groupValues[2].replace(Regex("\\s+"), " ")

        val embeddedMs = try {
            SimpleDateFormat("yyyy-MM-dd HH-mm-ss", Locale.US).parse(dateTimeStr)?.time
        } catch (e: Exception) {
            null
        }

        // Phone-number-like: after stripping spaces/dashes/parens, the
        // prefix is all digits (optional leading +), 7-15 digits long.
        val stripped = prefix.replace(Regex("[\\s\\-()]"), "")
        val isPhoneLike = stripped.matches(Regex("^\\+?[0-9]{7,15}$"))

        return if (isPhoneLike) {
            ParsedFilename(true, normalizePhoneForMatch(prefix), embeddedMs)
        } else {
            ParsedFilename(false, null, embeddedMs)
        }
    }

    /**
     * v19 — strips all non-digit characters and returns the LAST 10
     * digits (Indian mobile numbers), absorbing +91/91/0-prefix
     * inconsistencies between how CallLog reports a number and how the
     * recorder app wrote it into the filename. Used for both. If fewer
     * than 10 digits remain, returns the stripped string as-is — the
     * comparison will simply fail to match, which is correct (better than
     * a false positive).
     */
    private fun normalizePhoneForMatch(raw: String): String {
        val digits = raw.filter { it.isDigit() }
        return if (digits.length >= 10) digits.takeLast(10) else digits
    }

    /**
     * v19 — scans the configured folder ONCE per sync run (same
     * RELATIVE_PATH-substring filter and normalizeConfiguredFolderPath()
     * as v0.5, unchanged) and classifies every candidate file by its own
     * filename into numberIndex / nameCandidates. Replaces the old
     * per-call findRecordingFileNear() MediaStore query.
     */
    private fun scanRecordingFolder(folderPath: String?): FolderScanResult {
        val folder = normalizeConfiguredFolderPath(folderPath ?: "")
        val projection = arrayOf(
            MediaStore.Audio.Media._ID,
            MediaStore.Audio.Media.DISPLAY_NAME,
            MediaStore.Audio.Media.RELATIVE_PATH,
            MediaStore.Audio.Media.DATE_MODIFIED,
            MediaStore.Audio.Media.DATE_ADDED,
            MediaStore.Audio.Media.DURATION
        )
        val cursor = contentResolver.query(
            MediaStore.Audio.Media.EXTERNAL_CONTENT_URI,
            projection,
            null,
            null,
            null
        ) ?: return FolderScanResult(0, 0, emptyMap(), emptyList())

        var totalAudioFiles = 0
        var candidatesInFolder = 0
        val numberIndex = mutableMapOf<String, MutableList<RecordingFile>>()
        val nameCandidates = mutableListOf<Pair<RecordingFile, Long>>()

        cursor.use {
            val idIdx = it.getColumnIndex(MediaStore.Audio.Media._ID)
            val nameIdx = it.getColumnIndex(MediaStore.Audio.Media.DISPLAY_NAME)
            val relPathIdx = it.getColumnIndex(MediaStore.Audio.Media.RELATIVE_PATH)
            val dateModIdx = it.getColumnIndex(MediaStore.Audio.Media.DATE_MODIFIED)
            val dateAddIdx = it.getColumnIndex(MediaStore.Audio.Media.DATE_ADDED)
            val durationIdx = it.getColumnIndex(MediaStore.Audio.Media.DURATION)
            while (it.moveToNext()) {
                totalAudioFiles++
                val relPath = (if (relPathIdx >= 0) it.getString(relPathIdx) ?: "" else "").trim('/', ' ')
                if (folder.isNotBlank() && !relPath.contains(folder, ignoreCase = true)) continue
                candidatesInFolder++

                val name = if (nameIdx >= 0) it.getString(nameIdx) ?: "" else ""
                val parsed = parseRecordingFilename(name)
                if (parsed == null) {
                    Log.d(LOG_TAG, "Unparseable recording filename in configured folder, skipped: '$name'")
                    continue
                }

                val dateModMs = (if (dateModIdx >= 0) it.getLong(dateModIdx) else 0L) * 1000L
                val dateAddMs = (if (dateAddIdx >= 0) it.getLong(dateAddIdx) else 0L) * 1000L
                val durationMs = if (durationIdx >= 0 && !it.isNull(durationIdx)) it.getLong(durationIdx) else null
                val id = it.getLong(idIdx)
                val recordingFile = RecordingFile(
                    name,
                    ContentUris.withAppendedId(MediaStore.Audio.Media.EXTERNAL_CONTENT_URI, id),
                    relPath, dateModMs, dateAddMs, durationMs, parsed.embeddedTimestampMs
                )

                if (parsed.isPhoneNumberPrefix && parsed.normalizedNumber != null) {
                    numberIndex.getOrPut(parsed.normalizedNumber) { mutableListOf() }.add(recordingFile)
                } else if (parsed.embeddedTimestampMs != null) {
                    nameCandidates.add(recordingFile to parsed.embeddedTimestampMs)
                } else {
                    Log.d(LOG_TAG, "Name-prefixed recording with unparseable embedded timestamp, skipped: '$name'")
                }
            }
        }

        return FolderScanResult(totalAudioFiles, candidatesInFolder, numberIndex, nameCandidates)
    }

    /** v19 — same-number tiebreak: picks the candidate whose OWN embedded
     *  filename timestamp is closest to targetMs. A candidate with no
     *  parseable embedded timestamp is treated as maximally distant so a
     *  candidate that DOES have one wins first. */
    private fun pickClosestByEmbeddedTimestamp(candidates: List<RecordingFile>, targetMs: Long): RecordingFile {
        return candidates.minByOrNull { file ->
            val ts = file.embeddedTimestampMs
            if (ts != null) abs(ts - targetMs) else Long.MAX_VALUE
        } ?: candidates.first()
    }

    /**
     * v19 — the two-tier per-call lookup. v20 — REWORKED from "number-tier
     * wins unconditionally whenever ANY candidate exists" into a proper
     * competition — see this file's v20 changelog for the real incident
     * that exposed the old behavior (a stale 2-day-old number-tier file
     * beat the correct, much closer name-tier file because the number
     * tier never had a time bound and never had to compete at all).
     *
     * numberCandidate: among number-tier files sharing this call's
     * normalized number, the one closest to targetMs by its own embedded
     * timestamp (same-number tiebreak, unchanged from v19) — but it only
     * QUALIFIES if that gap is <= NUMBER_MATCH_MAX_GAP_MS. Otherwise it's
     * treated as absent (null), same as if the number simply had no file.
     *
     * nameResult: name-tier files within FILE_MATCH_TOLERANCE_MS of
     * targetMs (unchanged from v19) — a single hit, 2+ hits (ambiguous,
     * neither picked), or none.
     *
     * Decision:
     *   - qualifying number candidate AND a single name candidate: closer
     *     one wins (exact ties favor the name candidate — arbitrary but
     *     deterministic, not expected to matter at millisecond
     *     resolution).
     *   - qualifying number candidate, name result is NONE or AMBIGUOUS:
     *     number wins outright, same as v19.
     *   - no qualifying number candidate, single name candidate: name
     *     wins outright.
     *   - no qualifying number candidate, name result AMBIGUOUS: skip as
     *     ambiguous, same as v19.
     *   - neither: no match, same as v19.
     */
    private fun matchCallToFile(normalizedCallNumber: String, targetMs: Long, scan: FolderScanResult): MatchOutcome {
        val numberCandidates = scan.numberIndex[normalizedCallNumber]
        var numberFile: RecordingFile? = null
        var numberGapMs: Long? = null
        if (!numberCandidates.isNullOrEmpty()) {
            numberFile = if (numberCandidates.size == 1) {
                numberCandidates[0]
            } else {
                pickClosestByEmbeddedTimestamp(numberCandidates, targetMs)
            }
            numberGapMs = numberFile?.embeddedTimestampMs?.let { abs(it - targetMs) }
        }
        // v20 — the fix: a number-tier file is no longer an automatic win
        // just for existing. It must also be within NUMBER_MATCH_MAX_GAP_MS.
        val numberQualifies = numberGapMs != null && numberGapMs <= NUMBER_MATCH_MAX_GAP_MS

        val withinTolerance = scan.nameCandidates.filter { (_, ts) -> abs(ts - targetMs) <= FILE_MATCH_TOLERANCE_MS }
        val nameAmbiguous = withinTolerance.size >= 2
        val nameSingle = if (withinTolerance.size == 1) withinTolerance[0] else null
        val nameGapMs = nameSingle?.let { abs(it.second - targetMs) }

        return when {
            numberQualifies && nameSingle != null -> {
                if (nameGapMs!! <= numberGapMs!!) {
                    MatchOutcome(
                        file = nameSingle.first, matchedBy = "filename timestamp (name-based)", matchedGapMs = nameGapMs,
                        ambiguous = false, ambiguousNames = emptyList(),
                        otherTier = "phone number", otherFile = numberFile, otherGapMs = numberGapMs
                    )
                } else {
                    MatchOutcome(
                        file = numberFile, matchedBy = "phone number", matchedGapMs = numberGapMs,
                        ambiguous = false, ambiguousNames = emptyList(),
                        otherTier = "filename timestamp (name-based)", otherFile = nameSingle.first, otherGapMs = nameGapMs
                    )
                }
            }
            numberQualifies ->
                MatchOutcome(
                    file = numberFile, matchedBy = "phone number", matchedGapMs = numberGapMs,
                    ambiguous = false, ambiguousNames = emptyList()
                )
            nameSingle != null ->
                MatchOutcome(
                    file = nameSingle.first, matchedBy = "filename timestamp (name-based)", matchedGapMs = nameGapMs,
                    ambiguous = false, ambiguousNames = emptyList(),
                    otherTier = if (numberFile != null) "phone number" else null, otherFile = numberFile, otherGapMs = numberGapMs
                )
            nameAmbiguous ->
                MatchOutcome(
                    file = null, matchedBy = null, ambiguous = true,
                    ambiguousNames = withinTolerance.map { it.first.displayName },
                    otherTier = if (numberFile != null) "phone number" else null, otherFile = numberFile, otherGapMs = numberGapMs
                )
            else ->
                MatchOutcome(
                    file = null, matchedBy = null, ambiguous = false, ambiguousNames = emptyList(),
                    otherTier = if (numberFile != null) "phone number" else null, otherFile = numberFile, otherGapMs = numberGapMs
                )
        }
    }

    /**
     * v20 — formats a millisecond gap for logging: "13s" for anything
     * under a minute, otherwise "Xd Yh Zm" (days/hours omitted when zero,
     * minutes always shown) — e.g. "2d 19h 13m". Display-only, not used
     * in any matching decision.
     */
    private fun formatGap(gapMs: Long): String {
        val totalSec = gapMs / 1000
        if (totalSec < 60) return "${totalSec}s"
        val days = totalSec / 86400
        val hours = (totalSec % 86400) / 3600
        val minutes = (totalSec % 3600) / 60
        val parts = mutableListOf<String>()
        if (days > 0) parts.add("${days}d")
        if (days > 0 || hours > 0) parts.add("${hours}h")
        parts.add("${minutes}m")
        return parts.joinToString(" ")
    }

    /**
     * v19 — a call stuck unresolved for more than WATERMARK_GIVEUP_MS
     * (15 days) from its OWN call timestamp should stop blocking the
     * watermark. Called at every skip site in syncRecordings() — not-
     * answered, ambiguous, no-file-found, permission-denied, and a
     * rejected/failed upload alike — not just one branch. Returns true if
     * this call should be given up on (watermark allowed to advance past
     * it); false if the normal "stop advancing" freeze still applies.
     */
    private fun giveUpIfStale(call: CallEntry): Boolean {
        val callAgeMs = System.currentTimeMillis() - call.timestampMs
        return callAgeMs > WATERMARK_GIVEUP_MS
    }

    private fun runSyncRecordings() {
        Toast.makeText(this, "Syncing…", Toast.LENGTH_SHORT).show()
        lifecycleScope.launch {
            val result = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
                syncRecordings()
            }
            // v8 — the full multi-line diagnostic log (skip reasons, gaps,
            // etc.) no longer has a screen to render into, but it's still
            // valuable for debugging real issues, as this whole project's
            // history has repeatedly shown — kept in Logcat rather than
            // discarded outright.
            Log.d(LOG_TAG, result)
            val summaryLine = result.substringBefore("\n\n")
            Snackbar.make(webView, summaryLine, Snackbar.LENGTH_LONG).show()
        }
    }

    private fun syncRecordings(): String {
        val log = StringBuilder()

        val token = securePrefs.getString(AppPrefs.KEY_TOKEN, "") ?: ""
        if (token.isBlank()) {
            return "No bearer token saved. Open Settings and tap Save Token first."
        }

        if (ContextCompat.checkSelfPermission(this, Manifest.permission.READ_CALL_LOG)
            != PackageManager.PERMISSION_GRANTED
        ) {
            return "READ_CALL_LOG not granted — cannot sync."
        }

        val storedWatermark = syncPrefs.getLong(AppPrefs.KEY_LAST_SYNCED_MS, -1L)
        val sinceMs = if (storedWatermark > 0) storedWatermark
                      else (System.currentTimeMillis() - FIRST_SYNC_LOOKBACK_MS)

        val calls = try {
            readCallLogSince(sinceMs)
        } catch (e: SecurityException) {
            return "SecurityException reading call log: ${e.message}"
        } catch (e: Exception) {
            return "Error reading call log: ${e.message}"
        }

        if (calls.isEmpty()) {
            return "0 calls checked — nothing new since last sync."
        }

        val reportResult = try {
            reportCalls(token, calls)
        } catch (e: IOException) {
            return "report-calls failed: ${e.message}"
        } catch (e: Exception) {
            return "report-calls error: ${e.message}"
        }

        log.appendLine("Configured recording folder: '${reportResult.recordingFolderPath ?: "(not set)"}'")

        val matchedByTimestamp = reportResult.matched.associateBy { it.callTimestamp }

        // v19 — folder scanned ONCE per sync run (not per call) and indexed
        // by filename-embedded phone number / name+timestamp. See
        // scanRecordingFolder()/matchCallToFile() and this file's v19
        // changelog note for why this replaced the old per-call
        // findRecordingFileNear() DATE_MODIFIED search.
        var folderPermissionDenied = false
        val scanResult = try {
            scanRecordingFolder(reportResult.recordingFolderPath)
        } catch (e: SecurityException) {
            folderPermissionDenied = true
            FolderScanResult(0, 0, emptyMap(), emptyList())
        }

        var uploaded = 0
        var skipped = 0
        // v0.6 — diagnostic counters, per Srikanth's explicit ask to report
        // back how many skips were duration=0 vs ambiguous vs genuinely no
        // file found, before considering Bug 1 fully fixed.
        var skippedNotAnswered = 0
        var skippedAmbiguous = 0
        var skippedNoFile = 0
        var skippedPermission = 0
        // v19 — replaces skippedDurationMismatch (gate removed, see
        // changelog). Counts calls given up on via giveUpIfStale(),
        // regardless of which skip reason triggered it — useful signal
        // for how often stuck calls are being abandoned rather than
        // retried forever.
        var skippedGaveUp = 0
        // watermark only advances through a contiguous run of fully-handled
        // calls (unmatched, or matched-and-uploaded) starting from sinceMs —
        // the moment we hit a matched call we can't find a file for or can't
        // upload, we stop advancing so the next sync retries it. Calls are
        // read oldest-first (readCallLogSince's ASC sort) specifically so
        // this watermark logic is monotonic. v19 — EXCEPT when
        // giveUpIfStale() fires (see each skip site below), in which case
        // the watermark is allowed to advance past that one stuck call.
        var watermarkMs = sinceMs
        var stopAdvancing = false

        for (call in calls) {
            val matched = matchedByTimestamp[call.timestampStr]
            if (matched == null) {
                // Unmatched — already logged server-side to call_log_staging,
                // nothing more to do for this entry.
                if (!stopAdvancing) watermarkMs = call.timestampMs
                continue
            }

            // v0.6 HARD RULE — confirmed root cause of the wrong-file bug:
            // a duration=0 call (missed/unanswered/instantly disconnected)
            // cannot have a legitimate recording. Never even search for a
            // candidate file for one — this is unconditional, not a
            // tolerance/ambiguity judgment call.
            if (call.durationSeconds == 0) {
                log.appendLine(
                    "Skipped — call not answered (duration 0s), no recording possible, " +
                    "for lead ${matched.leadId} at ${call.timestampStr}"
                )
                skipped++
                skippedNotAnswered++
                if (giveUpIfStale(call)) {
                    log.appendLine("  (exceeded 15-day retry window — giving up on this call, watermark advancing past it)")
                    if (!stopAdvancing) watermarkMs = call.timestampMs
                    skippedGaveUp++
                } else {
                    stopAdvancing = true
                }
                continue
            }

            val targetMs = call.timestampMs + call.durationSeconds * 1000L

            if (folderPermissionDenied) {
                log.appendLine("Skipped — no audio-file permission for lead ${matched.leadId} at ${call.timestampStr}")
                skipped++
                skippedPermission++
                if (giveUpIfStale(call)) {
                    log.appendLine("  (exceeded 15-day retry window — giving up on this call, watermark advancing past it)")
                    if (!stopAdvancing) watermarkMs = call.timestampMs
                    skippedGaveUp++
                } else {
                    stopAdvancing = true
                }
                continue
            }

            val normalizedCallNumber = normalizePhoneForMatch(call.number)
            val outcome = matchCallToFile(normalizedCallNumber, targetMs, scanResult)

            val file = outcome.file
            if (file == null) {
                if (outcome.ambiguous) {
                    // v0.6 — two (or more) candidates both within tolerance:
                    // exactly the ambiguity that let a personal call's
                    // recording get picked for a lead it didn't belong to.
                    // Never auto-pick one — skip and surface all of them.
                    log.appendLine(
                        "Skipped — AMBIGUOUS: ${outcome.ambiguousNames.size} name-based candidates within " +
                        "${FILE_MATCH_TOLERANCE_MS / 1000} sec tolerance for lead ${matched.leadId} at ${call.timestampStr}"
                    )
                    log.appendLine("  candidates: ${outcome.ambiguousNames.joinToString(", ")}")
                    // v20 — a phone-number candidate may also have existed
                    // here but been excluded (either it lost, or it simply
                    // exceeded NUMBER_MATCH_MAX_GAP_MS) — surfaced for the
                    // same reason the "beat" note is on a successful match:
                    // makes an incident diagnosable from the log alone.
                    if (outcome.otherFile != null) {
                        val otherGapDesc = outcome.otherGapMs?.let { formatGap(it) } ?: "gap unknown"
                        log.appendLine("  a ${outcome.otherTier} candidate also existed but was excluded ($otherGapDesc away): '${outcome.otherFile.displayName}'")
                    }
                    skippedAmbiguous++
                } else {
                    // v0.4/v19 — full diagnostic instead of a plain "no file
                    // found", now reported against embedded filename
                    // timestamps rather than DATE_MODIFIED/DATE_ADDED.
                    logFileMatchMiss(log, scanResult, matched.leadId, call.timestampStr, targetMs, normalizedCallNumber)
                    // v20 — same "excluded candidate" diagnostic as above,
                    // for the plain-miss case (e.g. a stale number-tier file
                    // existed but exceeded NUMBER_MATCH_MAX_GAP_MS and
                    // nothing else qualified either).
                    if (outcome.otherFile != null) {
                        val otherGapDesc = outcome.otherGapMs?.let { formatGap(it) } ?: "gap unknown"
                        log.appendLine("  a ${outcome.otherTier} candidate also existed but was excluded ($otherGapDesc away): '${outcome.otherFile.displayName}'")
                    }
                    skippedNoFile++
                }
                skipped++
                if (giveUpIfStale(call)) {
                    log.appendLine("  (exceeded 15-day retry window — giving up on this call, watermark advancing past it)")
                    if (!stopAdvancing) watermarkMs = call.timestampMs
                    skippedGaveUp++
                } else {
                    stopAdvancing = true
                }
                continue
            }

            // v19 — duration is informational only now; the v0.7 hard gate
            // (DURATION_MISMATCH_THRESHOLD) was removed completely this
            // session, per Srikanth's explicit instruction — see changelog.
            val fileDurationSec = file.durationMs?.let { it / 1000 }
            val durationNote = if (fileDurationSec != null) {
                " [call=${call.durationSeconds}s, file=${fileDurationSec}s, diff=${abs(call.durationSeconds - fileDurationSec)}s]"
            } else {
                " [call=${call.durationSeconds}s, file duration unknown]"
            }

            try {
                val ok = uploadRecording(token, file, matched.leadId, matched.callTimestamp, matched.durationSeconds)
                if (ok) {
                    uploaded++
                    // v20 — always logs the winning tier AND its actual gap
                    // (not just the tier name), plus — when the OTHER tier
                    // also had a candidate that lost the competition — that
                    // candidate and its gap too. This is exactly the
                    // information that would have caught today's real
                    // incident (a stale number-tier file winning over a
                    // much closer name-tier file) immediately from the log.
                    val matchGapDesc = outcome.matchedGapMs?.let { formatGap(it) } ?: "gap unknown"
                    var matchNote = "matched by ${outcome.matchedBy} ('${file.displayName}', $matchGapDesc from call end)"
                    if (outcome.otherFile != null) {
                        val otherGapDesc = outcome.otherGapMs?.let { formatGap(it) } ?: "gap unknown"
                        matchNote += " — beat ${outcome.otherTier} candidate ('${outcome.otherFile.displayName}', $otherGapDesc away)"
                    }
                    log.appendLine("Uploaded for lead ${matched.leadId} at ${call.timestampStr} — $matchNote$durationNote")
                    if (!stopAdvancing) watermarkMs = call.timestampMs
                } else {
                    log.appendLine("Upload rejected by server for lead ${matched.leadId} at ${call.timestampStr}$durationNote")
                    if (giveUpIfStale(call)) {
                        log.appendLine("  (exceeded 15-day retry window — giving up on this call, watermark advancing past it)")
                        if (!stopAdvancing) watermarkMs = call.timestampMs
                        skippedGaveUp++
                    } else {
                        stopAdvancing = true
                    }
                }
            } catch (e: Exception) {
                log.appendLine("Upload error for lead ${matched.leadId} at ${call.timestampStr}: ${e.message}")
                if (giveUpIfStale(call)) {
                    log.appendLine("  (exceeded 15-day retry window — giving up on this call, watermark advancing past it)")
                    if (!stopAdvancing) watermarkMs = call.timestampMs
                    skippedGaveUp++
                } else {
                    stopAdvancing = true
                }
            }
        }

        syncPrefs.edit().putLong(AppPrefs.KEY_LAST_SYNCED_MS, watermarkMs).apply()

        val summary = "${calls.size} calls checked, ${reportResult.matched.size} matched, " +
                "$uploaded uploaded, $skipped skipped " +
                "($skippedNotAnswered not-answered, $skippedAmbiguous ambiguous, " +
                "$skippedNoFile no-file-found, $skippedPermission no-permission, " +
                "$skippedGaveUp gave-up-15day)"
        log.insert(0, "$summary\n\n")
        return log.toString()
    }

    /**
     * v0.4 — writes the actual reason a match was skipped, instead of a
     * plain "no file found". v19 — rewritten against the new filename-
     * based signals: DATE_MODIFIED/DATE_ADDED are no longer the primary
     * matching field, so the diagnostic now reports the closest
     * name-based candidate's OWN embedded filename timestamp instead.
     * Distinguishes two different root causes (now reported to Logcat):
     *   1. candidatesInFolder == 0 — the folder-substring filter matched
     *      NOTHING (out of totalAudioFiles audio files MediaStore knows
     *      about at all). Also samples a few likely-recording paths so the
     *      actual on-device path convention is visible without guessing
     *      (sampleLikelyRecordingPaths()/sampleMostRecentAudioFiles(),
     *      unchanged from v0.4/v0.5).
     *   2. candidatesInFolder > 0 — files WERE found in the folder (and at
     *      least parsed), but neither the number tier nor the name tier
     *      produced a match. Reports the closest name-based candidate's
     *      own embedded timestamp and its signed gap against the target,
     *      even though it missed tolerance, so a real-world miss can be
     *      diagnosed instead of just reported as "skipped."
     */
    private fun logFileMatchMiss(
        log: StringBuilder,
        scan: FolderScanResult,
        leadId: String,
        callTimestampStr: String,
        targetMs: Long,
        normalizedCallNumber: String
    ) {
        val fmt = SimpleDateFormat("yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss", Locale.US)
        val targetReadable = fmt.format(Date(targetMs))

        if (scan.candidatesInFolder == 0) {
            log.appendLine(
                "Skipped — 0 files matched the configured folder (out of ${scan.totalAudioFiles} " +
                "audio files MediaStore knows about) for lead $leadId at $callTimestampStr, target=$targetReadable"
            )
            val samples = sampleLikelyRecordingPaths()
            if (samples.isEmpty()) {
                log.appendLine("  No call/record-like audio file found anywhere via MediaStore.")
            } else {
                log.appendLine("  Sample audio files that DO look call/record-related (actual paths on this device):")
                samples.forEach { log.appendLine("    $it") }
            }
            // v0.5 — separate question from the folder-match bug: does
            // MediaStore's index even contain today's newest files at all,
            // or is there an indexing lag? Independent of the folder-path
            // fix above, so this stays even after that fix lands.
            val recent = sampleMostRecentAudioFiles()
            if (recent.isEmpty()) {
                log.appendLine("  MediaStore reports 0 audio files total (unexpected).")
            } else {
                log.appendLine("  Most recent audio files MediaStore knows about (any folder, newest first):")
                recent.forEach { log.appendLine("    $it") }
            }
            return
        }

        log.appendLine(
            "Skipped — no filename match for lead $leadId at $callTimestampStr " +
            "(call number normalized='$normalizedCallNumber', target=$targetReadable, " +
            "${scan.candidatesInFolder} parseable candidate(s) in folder)"
        )

        val closestName = scan.nameCandidates.minByOrNull { (_, ts) -> abs(ts - targetMs) }
        if (closestName != null) {
            val (file, ts) = closestName
            val gapMs = abs(ts - targetMs)
            val direction = if (ts - targetMs >= 0) "late" else "early"
            log.appendLine(
                "  closest name-based candidate: '%s' (relPath=%s) — %.1f sec %s vs target (tolerance is %.0f sec)"
                    .format(file.displayName, file.relativePath, gapMs / 1000.0, direction, FILE_MATCH_TOLERANCE_MS / 1000.0)
            )
        } else {
            log.appendLine("  No name-based candidates with a parseable embedded timestamp were found in the folder.")
        }
    }

    private fun readCallLogSince(sinceMs: Long): List<CallEntry> {
        val entries = mutableListOf<CallEntry>()
        val projection = arrayOf(
            CallLog.Calls.NUMBER,
            CallLog.Calls.DURATION,
            CallLog.Calls.TYPE,
            CallLog.Calls.DATE
        )
        // Ascending (oldest first) — needed for syncRecordings()'s watermark
        // logic to advance monotonically. No LIMIT, same "Invalid token
        // LIMIT" avoidance as the v0.2 debug scan, but unbounded here since
        // we want every call since the watermark, not just the latest few.
        val cursor = contentResolver.query(
            CallLog.Calls.CONTENT_URI,
            projection,
            "${CallLog.Calls.DATE} > ?",
            arrayOf(sinceMs.toString()),
            "${CallLog.Calls.DATE} ASC"
        ) ?: return entries

        val dateFormat = SimpleDateFormat("yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss", Locale.US)
        cursor.use {
            val numberIdx = it.getColumnIndex(CallLog.Calls.NUMBER)
            val durationIdx = it.getColumnIndex(CallLog.Calls.DURATION)
            val typeIdx = it.getColumnIndex(CallLog.Calls.TYPE)
            val dateIdx = it.getColumnIndex(CallLog.Calls.DATE)
            while (it.moveToNext()) {
                val number = it.getString(numberIdx) ?: continue
                val durationSec = (it.getString(durationIdx) ?: "0").toIntOrNull() ?: 0
                val direction = callTypeToString(it.getInt(typeIdx))
                val dateMs = it.getLong(dateIdx)
                entries.add(CallEntry(number, dateMs, dateFormat.format(Date(dateMs)), durationSec, direction))
            }
        }
        return entries
    }

    /** POSTs to /api/telephony/report-calls. Body shape confirmed against
     *  the live app.py route: {"calls": [...]}, NOT a bare top-level array. */
    private fun reportCalls(token: String, calls: List<CallEntry>): ReportCallsResult {
        val callsArray = JSONArray()
        for (c in calls) {
            val obj = JSONObject()
            obj.put("number", c.number)
            obj.put("timestamp", c.timestampStr)
            obj.put("duration", c.durationSeconds)
            obj.put("direction", c.direction)
            callsArray.put(obj)
        }
        val bodyJson = JSONObject()
        bodyJson.put("calls", callsArray)

        val requestBody = bodyJson.toString().toRequestBody("application/json".toMediaType())
        val request = Request.Builder()
            .url("$BASE_URL/api/telephony/report-calls")
            .addHeader("Authorization", "Bearer $token")
            .post(requestBody)
            .build()

        httpClient.newCall(request).execute().use { response ->
            val responseText = response.body?.string() ?: ""
            if (!response.isSuccessful) {
                throw IOException("HTTP ${response.code}: $responseText")
            }
            val json = JSONObject(responseText)
            val folderPath = if (json.isNull("recording_folder_path")) null
                              else json.optString("recording_folder_path", null)
            val matchedArr = json.optJSONArray("matched") ?: JSONArray()
            val matchedList = mutableListOf<MatchedEntry>()
            for (i in 0 until matchedArr.length()) {
                val m = matchedArr.getJSONObject(i)
                matchedList.add(
                    MatchedEntry(
                        leadId = m.optString("lead_id"),
                        callTimestamp = m.optString("call_timestamp"),
                        durationSeconds = m.optInt("duration_seconds", 0)
                    )
                )
            }
            return ReportCallsResult(folderPath, matchedList)
        }
    }

    /** POSTs to /api/telephony/upload-recording. Multipart file field name
     *  confirmed against the live app.py route: "recording", NOT "file". */
    private fun uploadRecording(
        token: String,
        file: RecordingFile,
        leadId: String,
        callTimestamp: String,
        durationSeconds: Int
    ): Boolean {
        val bytes = contentResolver.openInputStream(file.uri)?.use { it.readBytes() }
            ?: throw IOException("Could not open recording file stream.")
        val fileBody = bytes.toRequestBody("audio/mpeg".toMediaType())

        val multipart = MultipartBody.Builder()
            .setType(MultipartBody.FORM)
            .addFormDataPart("recording", file.displayName, fileBody)
            .addFormDataPart("lead_id", leadId)
            .addFormDataPart("call_timestamp", callTimestamp)
            .addFormDataPart("duration", durationSeconds.toString())
            .build()

        val request = Request.Builder()
            .url("$BASE_URL/api/telephony/upload-recording")
            .addHeader("Authorization", "Bearer $token")
            .post(multipart)
            .build()

        httpClient.newCall(request).execute().use { response ->
            val responseText = response.body?.string() ?: ""
            if (!response.isSuccessful) {
                throw IOException("HTTP ${response.code}: $responseText")
            }
            val json = JSONObject(responseText)
            return json.optBoolean("success", false)
        }
    }

    /**
     * v0.5 — strips a leading external-storage-root prefix from an
     * admin-typed folder path before comparing it to MediaStore's
     * RELATIVE_PATH, which is ALWAYS relative to that root and never
     * includes it. Without this, a configured path like
     * "/storage/emulated/0/Music/Recordings/Call Recordings/" can never
     * match RELATIVE_PATH's "Music/Recordings/Call Recordings/" — root
     * cause of v0.4's "0 files matched the configured folder" diagnostic
     * (confirmed 2026-07-31: sample files printed were IN the configured
     * folder, so the comparison itself, not the folder value, was wrong).
     */
    private fun normalizeConfiguredFolderPath(raw: String): String {
        var p = raw.trim().trim('/', ' ')
        val storageRootPrefixes = listOf(
            "storage/emulated/0/",
            "storage/self/primary/",
            "sdcard/"
        )
        for (prefix in storageRootPrefixes) {
            if (p.startsWith(prefix, ignoreCase = true)) {
                p = p.substring(prefix.length)
                break
            }
        }
        return p.trim('/', ' ')
    }

    /**
     * v0.4 — diagnostic helper for the "0 candidates in folder" case only:
     * samples up to 5 audio files whose name or path loosely suggests a
     * call recording (same "call"/"record" substring heuristic as the
     * original Phase A debug scan), so the ACTUAL relative path this
     * phone/recorder app uses is visible without guessing. Never used to
     * decide a match — purely for diagnosing why the folder filter found
     * nothing.
     */
    private fun sampleLikelyRecordingPaths(limit: Int = 5): List<String> {
        val samples = mutableListOf<String>()
        val projection = arrayOf(
            MediaStore.Audio.Media.DISPLAY_NAME,
            MediaStore.Audio.Media.RELATIVE_PATH
        )
        val cursor = contentResolver.query(
            MediaStore.Audio.Media.EXTERNAL_CONTENT_URI, projection, null, null, null
        ) ?: return samples
        cursor.use {
            val nameIdx = it.getColumnIndex(MediaStore.Audio.Media.DISPLAY_NAME)
            val relPathIdx = it.getColumnIndex(MediaStore.Audio.Media.RELATIVE_PATH)
            while (it.moveToNext() && samples.size < limit) {
                val name = if (nameIdx >= 0) it.getString(nameIdx) ?: "" else ""
                val relPath = if (relPathIdx >= 0) it.getString(relPathIdx) ?: "" else ""
                val haystack = "$relPath $name".lowercase(Locale.US)
                if (haystack.contains("call") || haystack.contains("record")) {
                    samples.add("$name | path=$relPath")
                }
            }
        }
        return samples
    }

    /**
     * v0.5 — answers a separate question from the folder-comparison bug:
     * does MediaStore's index even contain today's newest files? Sorts
     * DESCENDING by DATE_MODIFIED and takes the first `limit` in Kotlin
     * (no SQL LIMIT in sortOrder — same defensive style as the v0.2 CallLog
     * fix, even though MediaStore's own provider hasn't shown that bug).
     * Unfiltered by folder — deliberately shows the newest files anywhere,
     * so a real indexing-lag issue would be visible even if the folder-path
     * fix above is somehow still wrong.
     */
    private fun sampleMostRecentAudioFiles(limit: Int = 5): List<String> {
        val results = mutableListOf<Pair<Long, String>>()
        val projection = arrayOf(
            MediaStore.Audio.Media.DISPLAY_NAME,
            MediaStore.Audio.Media.RELATIVE_PATH,
            MediaStore.Audio.Media.DATE_MODIFIED
        )
        val cursor = contentResolver.query(
            MediaStore.Audio.Media.EXTERNAL_CONTENT_URI, projection, null, null, null
        ) ?: return emptyList()
        val fmt = SimpleDateFormat("yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss", Locale.US)
        cursor.use {
            val nameIdx = it.getColumnIndex(MediaStore.Audio.Media.DISPLAY_NAME)
            val relPathIdx = it.getColumnIndex(MediaStore.Audio.Media.RELATIVE_PATH)
            val dateModIdx = it.getColumnIndex(MediaStore.Audio.Media.DATE_MODIFIED)
            while (it.moveToNext()) {
                val name = if (nameIdx >= 0) it.getString(nameIdx) ?: "" else ""
                val relPath = if (relPathIdx >= 0) it.getString(relPathIdx) ?: "" else ""
                val dateModMs = (if (dateModIdx >= 0) it.getLong(dateModIdx) else 0L) * 1000L
                results.add(dateModMs to "$name | path=$relPath | modified=${fmt.format(Date(dateModMs))}")
            }
        }
        return results.sortedByDescending { it.first }.take(limit).map { it.second }
    }
}

import android.Manifest
import android.content.Context
import android.content.Intent
import android.content.SharedPreferences
import android.content.pm.PackageManager
import android.net.ConnectivityManager
import android.net.NetworkCapabilities
import android.os.Build
import android.os.Bundle
import android.os.PowerManager
import android.provider.CallLog
import android.provider.MediaStore
import android.webkit.CookieManager
import android.webkit.WebView
import android.widget.Button
import android.widget.TextView
import android.widget.Toast
import android.view.View
import androidx.appcompat.app.AppCompatActivity
import androidx.core.content.ContextCompat
import androidx.lifecycle.lifecycleScope
import kotlinx.coroutines.Dispatchers
import kotlinx.coroutines.launch
import kotlinx.coroutines.withContext
import okhttp3.Request
import okhttp3.RequestBody.Companion.toRequestBody
import org.json.JSONObject
import java.io.IOException
import java.text.SimpleDateFormat
import java.util.Date
import java.util.Locale

class SettingsActivity : AppCompatActivity() {

    private lateinit var tokenStatus: TextView
    private lateinit var syncTokenButton: Button
    private lateinit var debugOutput: TextView
    private lateinit var shareReportButton: Button
    private lateinit var securePrefs: SharedPreferences

    override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
        super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)
        setContentView(R.layout.activity_settings)

        tokenStatus = findViewById(R.id.token_status)
        syncTokenButton = findViewById(R.id.btn_sync_token)
        debugOutput = findViewById(R.id.debug_output)
        shareReportButton = findViewById(R.id.btn_share_report)

        securePrefs = AppPrefs.securePrefs(this)
        refreshTokenStatus()

        findViewById<View>(R.id.btn_back).setOnClickListener {
            finish()
        }

        syncTokenButton.setOnClickListener {
            syncToken()
        }

        findViewById<Button>(R.id.btn_check_call_log).setOnClickListener {
            runDiagnosticScan()
        }

        shareReportButton.setOnClickListener {
            shareReport()
        }
    }

    private fun refreshTokenStatus() {
        val hasToken = !securePrefs.getString(AppPrefs.KEY_TOKEN, "").isNullOrBlank()
        tokenStatus.text = if (hasToken) {
            "Token synced ✓"
        } else {
            "Not synced yet — tap \"Sync my token\" above."
        }
    }

    // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    // v2 — Option C self-service token sync. Extracts this device's
    // existing CRM session cookie (set when the user logged in through
    // MainActivity's WebView) and POSTs it to /api/my-token, which
    // mints and returns this user's own fresh token — see app.py
    // v0.38's api_my_token() for the server side. Every call mints a
    // NEW token (raw values aren't recoverable once hashed server-
    // side), so this only ever runs on an explicit button tap, never
    // automatically.
    // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    private fun syncToken() {
        syncTokenButton.isEnabled = false
        tokenStatus.text = "Syncing…"
        lifecycleScope.launch {
            val result = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
                try {
                    val cookie = CookieManager.getInstance().getCookie(BASE_URL)
                    if (cookie.isNullOrBlank()) {
                        Result.failure<String>(
                            IOException("Not logged in — open the app's main screen and log in first.")
                        )
                    } else {
                        val request = Request.Builder()
                            .url("$BASE_URL/api/my-token")
                            .addHeader("Cookie", cookie)
                            .post("".toRequestBody(null))
                            .build()
                        httpClient.newCall(request).execute().use { response ->
                            val text = response.body?.string() ?: ""
                            if (!response.isSuccessful) {
                                Result.failure<String>(IOException("HTTP ${response.code}: $text"))
                            } else {
                                val token = JSONObject(text).optString("token", "")
                                if (token.isBlank()) {
                                    Result.failure<String>(IOException("Server response was missing a token."))
                                } else {
                                    Result.success(token)
                                }
                            }
                        }
                    }
                } catch (e: Exception) {
                    Result.failure(e)
                }
            }
            result.onSuccess { token ->
                securePrefs.edit().putString(AppPrefs.KEY_TOKEN, token).apply()
                Toast.makeText(this@SettingsActivity, "Token synced.", Toast.LENGTH_SHORT).show()
            }.onFailure { e ->
                Toast.makeText(
                    this@SettingsActivity,
                    "Couldn't sync token: ${e.message}",
                    Toast.LENGTH_LONG
                ).show()
            }
            refreshTokenStatus()
            syncTokenButton.isEnabled = true
        }
    }

    // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    // v3 — full device diagnostic report. The two original sections
    // (Call Log, Recording Folder Scan — appendCallLog/
    // appendRecordingFiles below) are UNCHANGED from v1/v2; the new
    // sections above them are additive only.
    // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    private fun runDiagnosticScan() {
        debugOutput.text = "Scanning…"
        shareReportButton.isEnabled = false
        lifecycleScope.launch {
            val result = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
                val sb = StringBuilder()

                sb.appendLine("=== Device ===")
                appendDeviceInfo(sb)

                sb.appendLine()
                sb.appendLine("=== App ===")
                appendAppInfo(sb)

                sb.appendLine()
                sb.appendLine("=== Permissions ===")
                appendPermissionInfo(sb)

                sb.appendLine()
                sb.appendLine("=== Battery Optimization ===")
                appendBatteryInfo(sb)

                sb.appendLine()
                sb.appendLine("=== WebView ===")
                appendWebViewInfo(sb)

                sb.appendLine()
                sb.appendLine("=== Network ===")
                appendNetworkInfo(sb)

                sb.appendLine()
                sb.appendLine("=== Call Log (last 10) ===")
                try {
                    if (ContextCompat.checkSelfPermission(this@SettingsActivity, Manifest.permission.READ_CALL_LOG)
                        != PackageManager.PERMISSION_GRANTED
                    ) {
                        sb.appendLine("READ_CALL_LOG not granted — skipping.")
                    } else {
                        appendCallLog(sb)
                    }
                } catch (e: SecurityException) {
                    sb.appendLine("SecurityException reading call log: ${e.message}")
                } catch (e: Exception) {
                    sb.appendLine("Error reading call log: ${e.message}")
                }

                sb.appendLine()
                sb.appendLine("=== Recording Folder Scan (MediaStore.Audio) ===")
                try {
                    appendRecordingFiles(sb)
                } catch (e: SecurityException) {
                    sb.appendLine("SecurityException scanning recordings: ${e.message}")
                } catch (e: Exception) {
                    sb.appendLine("Error scanning recordings: ${e.message}")
                }

                sb.toString()
            }
            debugOutput.text = result
            shareReportButton.isEnabled = true
        }
    }

    private fun appendDeviceInfo(sb: StringBuilder) {
        sb.appendLine("Manufacturer: ${Build.MANUFACTURER}")
        sb.appendLine("Model: ${Build.MODEL}")
        sb.appendLine("Android version: ${Build.VERSION.RELEASE} (API ${Build.VERSION.SDK_INT})")
    }

    private fun appendAppInfo(sb: StringBuilder) {
        try {
            val pInfo = packageManager.getPackageInfo(packageName, 0)
            val versionCode = if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.P) {
                pInfo.longVersionCode
            } else {
                @Suppress("DEPRECATION")
                pInfo.versionCode.toLong()
            }
            sb.appendLine("Version: ${pInfo.versionName} (code $versionCode)")
        } catch (e: Exception) {
            sb.appendLine("Could not read app version: ${e.message}")
        }
    }

    private fun appendPermissionInfo(sb: StringBuilder) {
        fun status(permission: String): String =
            if (ContextCompat.checkSelfPermission(this, permission) == PackageManager.PERMISSION_GRANTED)
                "GRANTED" else "DENIED"

        sb.appendLine("READ_CALL_LOG: ${status(Manifest.permission.READ_CALL_LOG)}")

        // Storage/media read permission: READ_MEDIA_AUDIO on Android 13+
        // (Tiramisu), READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE (maxSdkVersion=32) below that
        // — matches the two permissions actually declared for this in
        // AndroidManifest.xml.
        val mediaPermission = if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.TIRAMISU) {
            Manifest.permission.READ_MEDIA_AUDIO
        } else {
            Manifest.permission.READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE
        }
        sb.appendLine("Storage/media read (${mediaPermission.substringAfterLast('.')}): ${status(mediaPermission)}")

        if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.TIRAMISU) {
            sb.appendLine("POST_NOTIFICATIONS: ${status(Manifest.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS)}")
        } else {
            sb.appendLine("POST_NOTIFICATIONS: N/A (not required below Android 13)")
        }
        // RECORD_AUDIO deliberately NOT checked here — not declared in
        // this app's manifest, so a self-permission check would always
        // read DENIED and be misleading rather than informative.
    }

    private fun appendBatteryInfo(sb: StringBuilder) {
        try {
            val pm = getSystemService(Context.POWER_SERVICE) as PowerManager
            val exempt = pm.isIgnoringBatteryOptimizations(packageName)
            if (exempt) {
                sb.appendLine("Ignoring battery optimizations (exempt) ✓")
            } else {
                sb.appendLine(
                    "NOT exempt from battery optimization — a common cause of the " +
                        "app being killed or backgrounded unexpectedly on some OEMs."
                )
            }
        } catch (e: Exception) {
            sb.appendLine("Could not read battery optimization status: ${e.message}")
        }
    }

    private fun appendWebViewInfo(sb: StringBuilder) {
        try {
            val pkg = WebView.getCurrentWebViewPackage()
            if (pkg == null) {
                sb.appendLine("Could not determine WebView package.")
            } else {
                sb.appendLine("Package: ${pkg.packageName}")
                sb.appendLine("Version: ${pkg.versionName}")
            }
        } catch (e: Exception) {
            sb.appendLine("Could not read WebView package info: ${e.message}")
        }
    }

    private fun appendNetworkInfo(sb: StringBuilder) {
        try {
            val cm = getSystemService(Context.CONNECTIVITY_SERVICE) as ConnectivityManager
            val network = cm.activeNetwork
            val caps = network?.let { cm.getNetworkCapabilities(it) }
            if (caps == null) {
                sb.appendLine("Connected: No")
            } else {
                sb.appendLine("Connected: Yes")
                val type = when {
                    caps.hasTransport(NetworkCapabilities.TRANSPORT_WIFI) -> "WiFi"
                    caps.hasTransport(NetworkCapabilities.TRANSPORT_CELLULAR) -> "Cellular"
                    caps.hasTransport(NetworkCapabilities.TRANSPORT_ETHERNET) -> "Ethernet"
                    else -> "Other"
                }
                sb.appendLine("Connection type: $type")
            }
        } catch (e: Exception) {
            sb.appendLine("Could not read network state: ${e.message}")
        }
    }

    // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    // v3 — Share action. Sends the full current report text (device
    // section + call-log/recording scan) via the native share sheet, so
    // the user can hand it to Srikanth over WhatsApp/email/etc. without
    // typing or copy-pasting anything by hand.
    // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    private fun shareReport() {
        val text = debugOutput.text.toString()
        val intent = Intent(Intent.ACTION_SEND).apply {
            type = "text/plain"
            putExtra(Intent.EXTRA_SUBJECT, "CLS Pilot Diagnostic Report")
            putExtra(Intent.EXTRA_TEXT, text)
        }
        startActivity(Intent.createChooser(intent, "Share diagnostic report"))
    }

    // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    // v0.1/v0.2 — original call-log/recording-folder scan logic.
    // UNCHANGED from v1/v2 — byte-for-byte the same as before the v3
    // device-report expansion above; only their caller (runDiagnostic
    // Scan, formerly runCallLogScan) moved.
    // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    private fun appendCallLog(sb: StringBuilder) {
        val projection = arrayOf(
            CallLog.Calls.NUMBER,
            CallLog.Calls.DURATION,
            CallLog.Calls.TYPE,
            CallLog.Calls.DATE
        )
        // Some OEM CallLog providers reject a "LIMIT n" suffix appended to
        // sortOrder ("Invalid token LIMIT"), so sort only here and truncate
        // to 10 rows below instead of relying on SQL LIMIT.
        val cursor = contentResolver.query(
            CallLog.Calls.CONTENT_URI,
            projection,
            null,
            null,
            "${CallLog.Calls.DATE} DESC"
        )
        if (cursor == null) {
            sb.appendLine("Call log query returned null cursor.")
            return
        }
        cursor.use {
            if (it.count == 0) {
                sb.appendLine("No call log entries found.")
            }
            val numberIdx = it.getColumnIndex(CallLog.Calls.NUMBER)
            val durationIdx = it.getColumnIndex(CallLog.Calls.DURATION)
            val typeIdx = it.getColumnIndex(CallLog.Calls.TYPE)
            val dateIdx = it.getColumnIndex(CallLog.Calls.DATE)
            val dateFormat = SimpleDateFormat("yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss", Locale.US)
            var rowsRead = 0
            while (rowsRead < 10 && it.moveToNext()) {
                val number = it.getString(numberIdx) ?: "unknown"
                val duration = it.getString(durationIdx) ?: "0"
                val type = callTypeToString(it.getInt(typeIdx))
                val date = dateFormat.format(Date(it.getLong(dateIdx)))
                sb.appendLine("$date | $type | $number | ${duration}s")
                rowsRead++
            }
        }
    }

    private fun appendRecordingFiles(sb: StringBuilder) {
        val projection = arrayOf(
            MediaStore.Audio.Media._ID,
            MediaStore.Audio.Media.DISPLAY_NAME,
            MediaStore.Audio.Media.RELATIVE_PATH,
            MediaStore.Audio.Media.DATA
        )
        val cursor = contentResolver.query(
            MediaStore.Audio.Media.EXTERNAL_CONTENT_URI,
            projection,
            null,
            null,
            null
        )
        if (cursor == null) {
            sb.appendLine("MediaStore query returned null cursor.")
            return
        }
        var found = 0
        cursor.use {
            val nameIdx = it.getColumnIndex(MediaStore.Audio.Media.DISPLAY_NAME)
            val relPathIdx = it.getColumnIndex(MediaStore.Audio.Media.RELATIVE_PATH)
            val dataIdx = it.getColumnIndex(MediaStore.Audio.Media.DATA)
            while (it.moveToNext()) {
                val name = if (nameIdx >= 0) it.getString(nameIdx) ?: "" else ""
                val relPath = if (relPathIdx >= 0) it.getString(relPathIdx) ?: "" else ""
                val data = if (dataIdx >= 0) it.getString(dataIdx) ?: "" else ""
                val haystack = "$relPath $data".lowercase(Locale.US)
                if (haystack.contains("call") || haystack.contains("record")) {
                    found++
                    sb.appendLine("$name | path=$relPath | data=$data")
                }
            }
        }
        if (found == 0) {
            sb.appendLine("No accessible recording files found.")
        }
    }
}
