```kotlin
package com.asianproperties.clspilot

/**
 * PunchActivity.kt — v3 (2026-08-06, APX Attendance Chunk A)
 *
 * Changelog:
 * v3 (Chunk A — photo compression + map overlay) — this file no longer
 *      draws ANY text watermark onto the captured photo. drawWatermark()
 *      is removed outright, along with its Canvas/Paint/Color imports.
 *      Reason: the server (cls_attendance_photo.py v1.0, called from
 *      app.py v0.35's punch-in/punch-out routes) now composites a
 *      Google Static Maps pin thumbnail + a coordinates/date-time text
 *      block onto the photo itself, falling back to the OLD plain-text
 *      style if the Maps call fails — drawing text here too would mean
 *      the server's map thumbnail lands on top of an already-burned-in
 *      watermark. This file's only remaining photo-processing job is
 *      resizeAndCompressForUpload() (replacing the old fixed-quality,
 *      no-resize compress call): caps the longest side at
 *      MAX_DIMENSION_PX and steps JPEG quality down only as far as
 *      needed to land the upload in the ~150-400KB target range (see
 *      that function's own doc comment), instead of uploading an
 *      unresized ~2.5MB selfie. No new Android dependency — resize/
 *      compress both use built-in Bitmap APIs.
 * v2 (Build Order Step 6) — a successful punch now also schedules/
 *      cancels AttendanceWorker.kt's hourly location ping: handles the
 *      success branch of submitPunch() by calling
 *      handlePostPunchWorkScheduling() (mode=="in" schedules the unique
 *      periodic work + separately requests ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION;
 *      mode=="out" cancels it). See that method's own doc comment for
 *      why the background-location request is deliberately its OWN,
 *      separate ActivityResultContracts.RequestPermission() call, fired
 *      only after a successful punch-in — never bundled with v1's
 *      CAMERA/ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION request in onCreate(). No other
 *      change to this file's v1 camera/GPS/watermark/upload flow.
 * v1 (Build Order Step 5) — initial version.
 *
 * Launched from MainActivity's AndroidBridge (punchIn()/punchOut()) with an
 * intent extra deciding which of the two it is — EXTRA_MODE = "in" or "out".
 * Everything below is shared between both modes except which endpoint gets
 * called and whether a late/on-time result is shown (punch-out has no
 * late/status concept — see cls_db.py v2.42's record_punch() docstring).
 *
 * FLOW
 * ----
 *   1. onCreate(): request CAMERA + ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION (this Activity's
 *      OWN concern — MainActivity's requestPermissionsIfNeeded() only
 *      handles the Telephony pilot's READ_CALL_LOG/READ_MEDIA_AUDIO, and
 *      stays that way; this is a materially different permission set for a
 *      materially different feature).
 *   2. CameraX front-camera preview starts as soon as CAMERA is granted.
 *   3. A SINGLE high-accuracy GPS fix is requested as soon as
 *      ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION is granted (FusedLocationProviderClient.
 *      getCurrentLocation() — one-shot, not a location stream/subscription;
 *      this Activity has no need for continuous updates).
 *   4. The Punch In/Out button stays DISABLED until BOTH the camera is
 *      bound AND a GPS fix has actually been obtained — never enabled
 *      "optimistically." This is the hard guarantee behind "never silently
 *      submit without coordinates": there is no code path that can reach
 *      the upload without lastLocation being non-null. A GPS failure shows
 *      a visible error + "Retry Location" button, never a silent fallback.
 *   5. On tap: takePicture() captures an in-memory JPEG (ImageCapture.
 *      OnImageCapturedCallback — no OutputFileOptions, so nothing is EVER
 *      written to the camera roll or any app-local file for this photo).
 *      No watermark is drawn client-side (see v3 changelog above) — the
 *      raw decoded Bitmap goes straight to resizing/compression.
 *   6. resizeAndCompressForUpload() caps the longest side and JPEG-
 *      compresses straight into an in-memory ByteArray (~150-400KB
 *      target), which is multipart-POSTed to /api/attendance/punch-in or
 *      punch-out, using the SAME stored bearer token as Telephony
 *      (AppPrefs.securePrefs(), KEY_TOKEN — no second token store; see
 *      cls_db.py v2.42's corrected user_api_tokens comment on the server
 *      side, which now documents this same token gating both features).
 *      The ByteArray is never written to disk — "no local file retention
 *      beyond what's needed to build the upload" is satisfied by never
 *      creating a file in the first place, not by a delete-after-upload
 *      step. The server now does the watermarking (cls_attendance_photo.
 *      py, called from app.py v0.35) before saving to disk.
 *   7. Server response ({success, status, late_minutes, geofence_breach}
 *      for punch-in; {success, geofence_breach} for punch-out — see
 *      app.py v0.30's 2 new routes) is shown as a Toast, then this
 *      Activity finishes back to the WebView, which the CRM's own
 *      /attendance page reloads to reflect the new status (no explicit
 *      reload call needed here — that page's own next load just reads
 *      the freshly-written attendance row).
 *
 * WHAT'S GENUINELY UNTESTED WITHOUT A PHYSICAL PHONE
 * ---------------------------------------------------
 * This environment has no Android SDK/emulator/device — nothing below was
 * ever actually run. What IS checked: Kotlin compiles conceptually against
 * the API shapes used (cross-referenced against CameraX/Play-Services-
 * Location's documented public API — see build.gradle's v2 comment on
 * versions), the manifest is well-formed, and every server-facing detail
 * (endpoint paths, multipart field names "photo"/"lat"/"lng"/"client_ts",
 * the Authorization header, the JSON response keys) is copied character-
 * for-character from app.py v0.30's actual route bodies, not guessed.
 * NOT verified, and genuinely needing a real device before this ships:
 *   - CameraX actually binding/previewing on real hardware (front-camera
 *     availability, rotation/mirroring quirks vary by OEM).
 *   - A real GPS fix's timing/accuracy indoors vs outdoors, and whether
 *     GPS_FIX_TIMEOUT_MS (below) is a sane wait before showing "retry."
 *   - The watermark's actual on-screen legibility/positioning against a
 *     real photo's varying brightness/contrast.
 *   - Real multipart upload over a real mobile connection (timeouts,
 *     retries on flaky signal — none of that exists yet, flagged, not
 *     built, since it wasn't asked for this step).
 *   - Runtime permission dialog behavior across OEM Android skins.
 *
 * NOT BUILT HERE (explicitly out of scope for this step):
 *   - AttendanceWorker.kt / WorkManager hourly location ping — Step 6.
 *   - FCM push handling — separate FCM-wiring step, needs Firebase setup.
 *   - Any retry/offline-queue for a failed upload — a failed punch today
 *     just shows the error and lets the user tap Punch In/Out again.
 */

import android.Manifest
import android.content.SharedPreferences
import android.content.pm.PackageManager
import android.graphics.Bitmap
import android.graphics.BitmapFactory
import android.graphics.Matrix
import android.location.Location
import android.os.Bundle
import android.util.Log
import android.view.View
import android.widget.Button
import android.widget.ProgressBar
import android.widget.TextView
import android.widget.Toast
import androidx.activity.result.contract.ActivityResultContracts
import androidx.appcompat.app.AppCompatActivity
import androidx.camera.core.CameraSelector
import androidx.camera.core.ImageCapture
import androidx.camera.core.ImageCaptureException
import androidx.camera.core.ImageProxy
import androidx.camera.core.Preview
import androidx.camera.lifecycle.ProcessCameraProvider
import androidx.camera.view.PreviewView
import androidx.core.content.ContextCompat
import androidx.lifecycle.lifecycleScope
import com.google.android.gms.location.CurrentLocationRequest
import com.google.android.gms.location.LocationServices
import com.google.android.gms.location.Priority
import com.google.android.gms.tasks.CancellationTokenSource
import androidx.work.ExistingPeriodicWorkPolicy
import androidx.work.PeriodicWorkRequestBuilder
import androidx.work.WorkManager
import kotlinx.coroutines.Dispatchers
import kotlinx.coroutines.launch
import kotlinx.coroutines.withContext
import okhttp3.MediaType.Companion.toMediaType
import okhttp3.MultipartBody
import okhttp3.OkHttpClient
import okhttp3.Request
import okhttp3.RequestBody.Companion.toRequestBody
import org.json.JSONObject
import java.io.ByteArrayOutputStream
import java.io.IOException
import java.text.SimpleDateFormat
import java.util.Date
import java.util.Locale
import java.util.concurrent.ExecutorService
import java.util.concurrent.Executors
import java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit

class PunchActivity : AppCompatActivity() {

    companion object {
        const val EXTRA_MODE = "mode"   // "in" or "out" — anything else defaults to "in"
        private const val LOG_TAG = "CLSPilotPunch"
        private const val BASE_URL = "https://crm.asianbuild.in"

        // Proposed default, flagged (same posture as MainActivity's
        // FILE_MATCH_TOLERANCE_MS/FIRST_SYNC_LOOKBACK_MS): how long to wait
        // for a high-accuracy fix before showing "couldn't get GPS, retry"
        // rather than leaving the user staring at a spinner forever. No
        // real on-device timing data exists yet to calibrate this.
        private const val GPS_FIX_TIMEOUT_MS = 20000L

        // resizeAndCompressForUpload() targets — proposed, flagged (same
        // "not measured against a real file" posture as GPS_FIX_TIMEOUT_MS
        // above; this environment has no device to test against). Longest
        // side is capped at MAX_DIMENSION_PX (never upscaled) before any
        // quality reduction, since resizing removes far more bytes than
        // lowering quality does for the same loss of legibility. Quality
        // then steps down from the starting value only as far as needed to
        // land under TARGET_MAX_BYTES, never below QUALITY_FLOOR — an
        // admin reviewing a geofence breach still needs a legible face.
        private const val MAX_DIMENSION_PX = 1280
        private const val TARGET_MAX_BYTES = 400 * 1024
        private const val JPEG_QUALITY_START = 80
        private const val JPEG_QUALITY_STEP = 10
        private const val JPEG_QUALITY_FLOOR = 40
    }

    private lateinit var mode: String
    private lateinit var previewView: PreviewView
    private lateinit var statusText: TextView
    private lateinit var captureButton: Button
    private lateinit var retryLocationButton: Button
    private lateinit var progressBar: ProgressBar
    private lateinit var securePrefs: SharedPreferences

    private val httpClient = OkHttpClient()
    private var cameraExecutor: ExecutorService? = null
    private var imageCapture: ImageCapture? = null
    private var lastLocation: Location? = null
    private var cancellationTokenSource: CancellationTokenSource? = null

    private val cameraPermissionLauncher =
        registerForActivityResult(ActivityResultContracts.RequestPermission()) { granted ->
            if (granted) {
                startCamera()
            } else {
                statusText.text = "Camera permission denied — cannot punch ${modeLabel()} without a photo."
            }
        }

    private val locationPermissionLauncher =
        registerForActivityResult(ActivityResultContracts.RequestPermission()) { granted ->
            if (granted) fetchLocation() else onLocationFailed("Location permission denied.")
        }

    override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
        super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)
        setContentView(R.layout.activity_punch)

        mode = if (intent.getStringExtra(EXTRA_MODE) == "out") "out" else "in"
        title = if (mode == "out") "Punch Out" else "Punch In"

        securePrefs = AppPrefs.securePrefs(this)
        cameraExecutor = Executors.newSingleThreadExecutor()

        previewView = findViewById(R.id.preview_view)
        statusText = findViewById(R.id.status_text)
        captureButton = findViewById(R.id.btn_capture)
        retryLocationButton = findViewById(R.id.btn_retry_location)
        progressBar = findViewById(R.id.progress_bar)

        captureButton.text = if (mode == "out") "Punch Out" else "Punch In"
        captureButton.isEnabled = false
        retryLocationButton.visibility = View.GONE
        statusText.text = "Starting camera and getting your location…"

        findViewById<View>(R.id.btn_cancel).setOnClickListener { finish() }
        captureButton.setOnClickListener { onCaptureTapped() }
        retryLocationButton.setOnClickListener {
            retryLocationButton.visibility = View.GONE
            fetchLocation()
        }

        ensureCameraPermission()
        ensureLocationPermission()
    }

    override fun onDestroy() {
        super.onDestroy()
        cancellationTokenSource?.cancel()
        cameraExecutor?.shutdown()
    }

    // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    // Camera (CameraX, front lens, in-memory capture only)
    // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    private fun ensureCameraPermission() {
        if (ContextCompat.checkSelfPermission(this, Manifest.permission.CAMERA)
            == PackageManager.PERMISSION_GRANTED
        ) {
            startCamera()
        } else {
            cameraPermissionLauncher.launch(Manifest.permission.CAMERA)
        }
    }

    private fun startCamera() {
        val providerFuture = ProcessCameraProvider.getInstance(this)
        providerFuture.addListener({
            val provider = providerFuture.get()
            val preview = Preview.Builder().build().also {
                it.setSurfaceProvider(previewView.surfaceProvider)
            }
            val capture = ImageCapture.Builder().build()
            try {
                provider.unbindAll()
                provider.bindToLifecycle(this, CameraSelector.DEFAULT_FRONT_CAMERA, preview, capture)
                imageCapture = capture
            } catch (e: Exception) {
                Log.e(LOG_TAG, "Camera bind failed: ${e.message}")
                statusText.text = "Could not start the front camera: ${e.message}"
            }
            updateCaptureButtonEnabled()
        }, ContextCompat.getMainExecutor(this))
    }

    // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    // Location (single high-accuracy fix, never a stream/subscription)
    // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    private fun ensureLocationPermission() {
        if (ContextCompat.checkSelfPermission(this, Manifest.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION)
            == PackageManager.PERMISSION_GRANTED
        ) {
            fetchLocation()
        } else {
            locationPermissionLauncher.launch(Manifest.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION)
        }
    }

    private fun fetchLocation() {
        if (ContextCompat.checkSelfPermission(this, Manifest.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION)
            != PackageManager.PERMISSION_GRANTED
        ) {
            onLocationFailed("Location permission not granted.")
            return
        }
        statusText.text = "Getting your location…"
        progressBar.visibility = View.VISIBLE
        lastLocation = null
        updateCaptureButtonEnabled()

        val request = CurrentLocationRequest.Builder()
            .setPriority(Priority.PRIORITY_HIGH_ACCURACY)
            .setDurationMillis(GPS_FIX_TIMEOUT_MS)
            .build()
        val cts = CancellationTokenSource()
        cancellationTokenSource = cts

        try {
            LocationServices.getFusedLocationProviderClient(this)
                .getCurrentLocation(request, cts.token)
                .addOnSuccessListener { location -> onLocationResult(location) }
                .addOnFailureListener { e -> onLocationFailed("GPS error: ${e.message}") }
        } catch (e: SecurityException) {
            onLocationFailed("Location permission not granted.")
        }
    }

    private fun onLocationResult(location: Location?) {
        progressBar.visibility = View.GONE
        if (location == null) {
            // getCurrentLocation() completing with a null result (timeout,
            // no fix obtained) is the documented failure mode for this
            // API — treated identically to an exception: visible error +
            // retry, never a silent "proceed anyway."
            onLocationFailed("Couldn't get a GPS fix — make sure Location is on and try again.")
            return
        }
        lastLocation = location
        statusText.text = "Location ready (accuracy ±${location.accuracy.toInt()}m). " +
                "Tap Punch ${modeCapitalized()} when you're ready."
        updateCaptureButtonEnabled()
    }

    private fun onLocationFailed(message: String) {
        progressBar.visibility = View.GONE
        lastLocation = null
        statusText.text = message
        retryLocationButton.visibility = View.VISIBLE
        updateCaptureButtonEnabled()
    }

    // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    // Capture button gating — the actual "never silently submit
    // without coordinates" guarantee lives here: the button is simply
    // never enabled unless lastLocation is non-null.
    // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    private fun updateCaptureButtonEnabled() {
        captureButton.isEnabled = imageCapture != null && lastLocation != null
    }

    private fun onCaptureTapped() {
        val capture = imageCapture
        val location = lastLocation
        if (capture == null || location == null) {
            // Defense-in-depth only — the button should already be
            // disabled in this state; this guards against a stray tap
            // event racing a permission/GPS-loss change.
            Toast.makeText(this, "Not ready yet — camera and GPS are both required.", Toast.LENGTH_SHORT).show()
            return
        }
        val token = securePrefs.getString(AppPrefs.KEY_TOKEN, "") ?: ""
        if (token.isBlank()) {
            Toast.makeText(this, "No app token saved — open Settings and save one first.", Toast.LENGTH_LONG).show()
            return
        }

        captureButton.isEnabled = false
        retryLocationButton.isEnabled = false
        progressBar.visibility = View.VISIBLE
        statusText.text = "Capturing photo…"

        capture.takePicture(
            ContextCompat.getMainExecutor(this),
            object : ImageCapture.OnImageCapturedCallback() {
                override fun onCaptureSuccess(image: ImageProxy) {
                    val bitmap = imageProxyToBitmap(image)
                    image.close()
                    if (bitmap == null) {
                        onSubmitFailed("Could not decode the captured photo.")
                        return
                    }
                    submitPunch(token, bitmap, location)
                }

                override fun onError(exception: ImageCaptureException) {
                    onSubmitFailed("Camera capture failed: ${exception.message}")
                }
            }
        )
    }

    /** In-memory JPEG decode (no OutputFileOptions was used — takePicture()
     *  never wrote anything to disk). Corrects rotation only; front-camera
     *  mirroring is left as CameraX/the device driver produces it — not
     *  verified on a real device (see this file's header note). */
    private fun imageProxyToBitmap(image: ImageProxy): Bitmap? {
        val buffer = image.planes[0].buffer
        val bytes = ByteArray(buffer.remaining())
        buffer.get(bytes)
        val decoded = BitmapFactory.decodeByteArray(bytes, 0, bytes.size) ?: return null
        val rotation = image.imageInfo.rotationDegrees
        if (rotation == 0) return decoded
        val matrix = Matrix().apply { postRotate(rotation.toFloat()) }
        return Bitmap.createBitmap(decoded, 0, 0, decoded.width, decoded.height, matrix, true)
    }

    /**
     * Caps the longest side at MAX_DIMENSION_PX (never upscales a smaller
     * photo), then JPEG-compresses into an in-memory ByteArray, stepping
     * quality down from JPEG_QUALITY_START in JPEG_QUALITY_STEP
     * increments — but never below JPEG_QUALITY_FLOOR — until the result
     * is under TARGET_MAX_BYTES or the floor is reached, whichever comes
     * first. Resize is the primary size lever (dominates the byte count
     * far more than quality does); the quality loop is a safety net for
     * an unusually detailed/bright scene that's still too large after
     * resizing alone. No watermark is drawn here (see this file's v3
     * changelog note) — the server draws it after upload.
     *
     * CPU-bound — callers should run this off the main thread (submitPunch()
     * does, via Dispatchers.Default).
     */
    private fun resizeAndCompressForUpload(source: Bitmap): ByteArray {
        val longestSide = maxOf(source.width, source.height)
        val scale = if (longestSide > MAX_DIMENSION_PX) MAX_DIMENSION_PX.toFloat() / longestSide else 1f
        val resized = if (scale < 1f) {
            Bitmap.createScaledBitmap(
                source,
                (source.width * scale).toInt().coerceAtLeast(1),
                (source.height * scale).toInt().coerceAtLeast(1),
                true
            )
        } else source

        var quality = JPEG_QUALITY_START
        var bytes: ByteArray
        while (true) {
            bytes = ByteArrayOutputStream().also {
                resized.compress(Bitmap.CompressFormat.JPEG, quality, it)
            }.toByteArray()
            if (bytes.size <= TARGET_MAX_BYTES || quality <= JPEG_QUALITY_FLOOR) break
            quality -= JPEG_QUALITY_STEP
        }
        Log.d(LOG_TAG, "resizeAndCompressForUpload: ${source.width}x${source.height} -> " +
                "${resized.width}x${resized.height} @ q$quality = ${bytes.size} bytes")
        return bytes
    }

    // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    // Upload — same multipart-with-bearer-token pattern as
    // MainActivity's uploadRecording(); endpoint path, field names, and
    // response keys are copied from app.py v0.30's actual route bodies.
    // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    private fun submitPunch(token: String, bitmap: Bitmap, location: Location) {
        lifecycleScope.launch {
            statusText.text = "Uploading…"
            val clientTs = SimpleDateFormat("yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss", Locale.US).format(Date())
            try {
                // JPEG bytes live only in this local val — never written
                // to a file anywhere, satisfying "no local file retention
                // beyond what's needed to build the upload." Resize/
                // compress is CPU-bound (Dispatchers.Default); the actual
                // network call is the separate Dispatchers.IO step below.
                val jpegBytes = withContext(Dispatchers.Default) {
                    resizeAndCompressForUpload(bitmap)
                }
                val response = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
                    uploadPunch(token, jpegBytes, location, clientTs)
                }
                progressBar.visibility = View.GONE
                Log.d(LOG_TAG, "Punch $mode response: $response")

                val breachNote = if (response.optBoolean("geofence_breach", false))
                    " — OUTSIDE GEOFENCE (flagged for admin review)" else ""
                val timingNote = if (mode == "in") {
                    val status = response.optString("status", "recorded")
                    val late = response.optInt("late_minutes", 0)
                    if (late > 0) " — $status, $late min late" else " — $status"
                } else ""
                Toast.makeText(
                    this@PunchActivity,
                    "Punch ${modeLabel()} recorded$timingNote$breachNote",
                    Toast.LENGTH_LONG
                ).show()
                handlePostPunchWorkScheduling()
                setResult(RESULT_OK)
                finish()
            } catch (e: IOException) {
                onSubmitFailed("Upload failed: ${e.message}")
            } catch (e: Exception) {
                onSubmitFailed("Unexpected error: ${e.message}")
            }
        }
    }

    /** POSTs to /api/attendance/punch-in or /api/attendance/punch-out
     *  (mode decides which — "in"/"out" match the URL segment exactly).
     *  Multipart field names 'photo'/'lat'/'lng'/'client_ts' and the
     *  Authorization bearer header are confirmed against app.py v0.30's
     *  actual route bodies (_parse_punch_request()). */
    private fun uploadPunch(token: String, jpegBytes: ByteArray, location: Location, clientTs: String): JSONObject {
        val fileBody = jpegBytes.toRequestBody("image/jpeg".toMediaType())
        val multipart = MultipartBody.Builder()
            .setType(MultipartBody.FORM)
            .addFormDataPart("photo", "punch_$mode.jpg", fileBody)
            .addFormDataPart("lat", location.latitude.toString())
            .addFormDataPart("lng", location.longitude.toString())
            .addFormDataPart("client_ts", clientTs)
            .build()

        val request = Request.Builder()
            .url("$BASE_URL/api/attendance/punch-$mode")
            .addHeader("Authorization", "Bearer $token")
            .post(multipart)
            .build()

        httpClient.newCall(request).execute().use { response ->
            val text = response.body?.string() ?: ""
            if (!response.isSuccessful) {
                throw IOException("HTTP ${response.code}: $text")
            }
            return JSONObject(text)
        }
    }

    private fun onSubmitFailed(message: String) {
        progressBar.visibility = View.GONE
        statusText.text = message
        captureButton.isEnabled = true
        retryLocationButton.isEnabled = true
        Toast.makeText(this, message, Toast.LENGTH_LONG).show()
        Log.e(LOG_TAG, "Punch $mode failed: $message")
    }

    private fun modeLabel(): String = if (mode == "out") "out" else "in"
    private fun modeCapitalized(): String = if (mode == "out") "Out" else "In"

    // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    // Build Order Step 6 — AttendanceWorker scheduling. Called ONLY
    // after a successful punch (submitPunch()'s success branch), never
    // speculatively — an upload failure leaves any existing schedule
    // untouched rather than guessing at intent.
    // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    private val backgroundLocationPermissionLauncher =
        registerForActivityResult(ActivityResultContracts.RequestPermission()) { granted ->
            // Whether granted or not, the worker is already scheduled by
            // the time this callback fires (see handlePostPunchWorkScheduling()
            // below) — AttendanceWorker.doWork() already treats "no fix
            // this run" as an ordinary, non-fatal outcome, so a denial
            // here doesn't need special handling beyond a log line.
            Log.d(LOG_TAG, "ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION ${if (granted) "granted" else "denied"}.")
        }

    /**
     * mode=="in": schedules the 60-minute AttendanceWorker (unique work,
     * ExistingPeriodicWorkPolicy.KEEP — if it's somehow already scheduled
     * from an earlier punch-in that never got a matching punch-out, this
     * does NOT reset its 60-minute timer), then — as its OWN, separate
     * step — requests ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION if not already granted.
     *
     * THIS IS DELIBERATELY NOT REQUESTED ALONGSIDE Step 5's CAMERA/
     * ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION ask in onCreate(), for two reasons: (1)
     * Android's own platform rule — requesting background location in
     * the same multi-permission prompt as a foreground location/other
     * permission is silently ignored by the OS, it MUST be its own
     * separate ActivityResultContracts.RequestPermission() call; (2)
     * even if that weren't a hard OS rule, firing it only now (after a
     * successful punch-in, a materially later point in the flow) keeps
     * the two asks visibly distinct to the user rather than one
     * overwhelming multi-permission dialog on first launch.
     *
     * mode=="out": cancels the unique work. A punch-out with no
     * matching prior punch-in (e.g. app data was cleared) just calls
     * cancelUniqueWork() on a name that was never scheduled — WorkManager
     * treats that as a harmless no-op, not an error.
     */
    private fun handlePostPunchWorkScheduling() {
        if (mode == "in") {
            scheduleAttendanceWorker()
            if (ContextCompat.checkSelfPermission(this, Manifest.permission.ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION)
                != PackageManager.PERMISSION_GRANTED
            ) {
                Toast.makeText(
                    this,
                    "For hourly location updates while you're punched in, please also allow background location.",
                    Toast.LENGTH_LONG
                ).show()
                backgroundLocationPermissionLauncher.launch(Manifest.permission.ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION)
            }
        } else {
            cancelAttendanceWorker()
        }
    }

    private fun scheduleAttendanceWorker() {
        val request = PeriodicWorkRequestBuilder<AttendanceWorker>(60, TimeUnit.MINUTES).build()
        WorkManager.getInstance(applicationContext).enqueueUniquePeriodicWork(
            AttendanceWorker.UNIQUE_WORK_NAME,
            ExistingPeriodicWorkPolicy.KEEP,
            request
        )
        Log.d(LOG_TAG, "AttendanceWorker scheduled (unique work '${AttendanceWorker.UNIQUE_WORK_NAME}').")
    }

    private fun cancelAttendanceWorker() {
        WorkManager.getInstance(applicationContext).cancelUniqueWork(AttendanceWorker.UNIQUE_WORK_NAME)
        Log.d(LOG_TAG, "AttendanceWorker cancelled (unique work '${AttendanceWorker.UNIQUE_WORK_NAME}').")
    }
}
```

```kotlin
package com.asianproperties.clspilot

/**
 * AttendanceWorker.kt — v1 (2026-08-02, APX Attendance v0.9 pilot, Build Order Step 6)
 *
 * WorkManager PeriodicWorkRequest, 60-minute interval, unique work name
 * (UNIQUE_WORK_NAME) — scheduled by PunchActivity.kt right after a
 * successful punch-in, cancelled right after a successful punch-out (see
 * PunchActivity.kt's scheduleAttendanceWorker()/cancelAttendanceWorker()).
 * Each run takes ONE single-fix location reading and POSTs it to
 * /api/attendance/location-ping — no continuous location subscription, no
 * foreground service, matching the v0.9 spec's "single-fix location ping"
 * description exactly.
 *
 * WHY A CoroutineWorker
 * ----------------------
 * doWork() needs to (a) read EncryptedSharedPreferences, (b) await an
 * async FusedLocationProviderClient callback, and (c) make a blocking
 * OkHttp call — all off the main thread. CoroutineWorker gives doWork()
 * suspend-function support directly (WorkManager runs it on its own
 * dispatcher already), so no extra Dispatchers.IO wrapping is needed here
 * the way PunchActivity.kt needs it (that file runs on lifecycleScope /
 * the main thread by default; this one doesn't).
 *
 * FAILURE POSTURE — EVERY failure path returns Result.success(), NEVER
 * Result.failure()
 * -----------------------------------------------------------------------
 * No token saved, no location permission, no GPS fix, server says "not
 * open" (silently no-op — cls_db.record_location_ping() already handles
 * that server-side) — all of these are ordinary, expected, non-error
 * outcomes for an hourly background ping. Result.retry() is used ONLY for
 * an actual network/IO failure (the request never reached the server or
 * got a malformed response) — WorkManager's built-in backoff handles
 * retrying that specific case. This mirrors this whole app's established
 * philosophy (MainActivity.kt's syncRecordings(): "never fail silently,"
 * but ALSO never treat an expected no-op as a failure needing a retry
 * storm).
 *
 * BACKGROUND LOCATION PERMISSION — NOT REQUESTED HERE
 * -----------------------------------------------------------------------
 * A Worker has no Activity/UI context, so it CANNOT show a permission
 * dialog itself. ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION is requested by PunchActivity
 * (its own separate ActivityResultContracts.RequestPermission() call,
 * fired only after a successful punch-in — see that file's header note on
 * why it's deliberately NOT bundled with Step 5's CAMERA/ACCESS_FINE_
 * LOCATION request). If it was never granted, getCurrentLocation() below
 * still runs but Android silently withholds a real fix while the app is
 * backgrounded — handled identically to "no fix this run": log and
 * Result.success(), never a crash, never a retry storm.
 *
 * WHAT'S GENUINELY UNTESTED WITHOUT A PHYSICAL PHONE
 * -----------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Same environment limitation as PunchActivity.kt (no Android SDK/
 * emulator/device here — see that file's header for what WAS checked:
 * endpoint path, JSON body keys, and the Authorization header below are
 * copied character-for-character from app.py v0.30's actual
 * api_attendance_location_ping() route, not guessed). NOT verified, and
 * genuinely needing a real device:
 *   - WorkManager actually firing on the real ~60-minute cadence Android
 *     grants a PeriodicWorkRequest (the OS may batch/delay this well
 *     beyond 60 minutes depending on Doze/battery-optimization state —
 *     expected OS behavior, not a bug in this code, but untested here).
 *   - Whether ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION actually yields a real fix from
 *     a Worker running while the app is fully backgrounded on a given
 *     OEM's Android build (some OEMs restrict background location more
 *     aggressively than stock Android).
 *   - Real network behavior on a flaky mobile connection triggering
 *     Result.retry()'s backoff in practice.
 *
 * NOT BUILT HERE (explicitly out of scope for this step):
 *   - Any admin-facing "last ping" visibility/diagnostics.
 *   - Battery-optimization exemption prompts (Doze can delay/skip runs;
 *     not addressed — flagged, not built, since it wasn't asked for).
 */

import android.Manifest
import android.content.Context
import android.content.pm.PackageManager
import android.location.Location
import android.util.Log
import androidx.core.content.ContextCompat
import androidx.work.CoroutineWorker
import androidx.work.WorkerParameters
import com.google.android.gms.location.CurrentLocationRequest
import com.google.android.gms.location.LocationServices
import com.google.android.gms.location.Priority
import com.google.android.gms.tasks.CancellationTokenSource
import kotlinx.coroutines.suspendCancellableCoroutine
import okhttp3.MediaType.Companion.toMediaType
import okhttp3.OkHttpClient
import okhttp3.Request
import okhttp3.RequestBody.Companion.toRequestBody
import org.json.JSONObject
import java.io.IOException
import java.text.SimpleDateFormat
import java.util.Date
import java.util.Locale
import kotlin.coroutines.resume
import kotlin.coroutines.resumeWithException

class AttendanceWorker(
    appContext: Context,
    params: WorkerParameters
) : CoroutineWorker(appContext, params) {

    companion object {
        const val UNIQUE_WORK_NAME = "attendance_location_ping"
        private const val LOG_TAG = "CLSPilotAttendanceWorker"
        private const val BASE_URL = "https://crm.asianbuild.in"

        // Same proposed-default posture as PunchActivity.kt's
        // GPS_FIX_TIMEOUT_MS — flagged, not measured against real
        // background-location timing.
        private const val GPS_FIX_TIMEOUT_MS = 20000L
    }

    private val httpClient = OkHttpClient()

    override suspend fun doWork(): Result {
        val securePrefs = AppPrefs.securePrefs(applicationContext)
        val token = securePrefs.getString(AppPrefs.KEY_TOKEN, "") ?: ""
        if (token.isBlank()) {
            Log.w(LOG_TAG, "No app token saved — skipping this run (not a failure).")
            return Result.success()
        }

        if (ContextCompat.checkSelfPermission(applicationContext, Manifest.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION)
            != PackageManager.PERMISSION_GRANTED
        ) {
            Log.w(LOG_TAG, "ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION not granted — skipping this run (not a failure).")
            return Result.success()
        }

        val location = try {
            fetchLocation()
        } catch (e: SecurityException) {
            Log.w(LOG_TAG, "SecurityException getting location: ${e.message} — skipping this run.")
            null
        } catch (e: Exception) {
            Log.w(LOG_TAG, "Location fetch failed: ${e.message} — skipping this run.")
            null
        }

        if (location == null) {
            // Covers: no GPS fix within timeout, and (per this file's
            // header note) the case where ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION was
            // never granted, so Android withholds a fix in the background
            // even though ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION itself is granted.
            Log.w(LOG_TAG, "No location fix this run — skipping (server also silently " +
                    "no-ops a ping with no open punch; this is belt-and-suspenders).")
            return Result.success()
        }

        return try {
            val accepted = postLocationPing(token, location)
            Log.d(LOG_TAG, "location-ping run complete — server accepted=$accepted")
            Result.success()
        } catch (e: IOException) {
            Log.e(LOG_TAG, "location-ping network/IO failure: ${e.message} — will retry.")
            Result.retry()
        }
    }

    /** Single high-accuracy fix — NOT a location stream/subscription.
     *  Wraps the Play-Services-Location callback API in a coroutine
     *  directly (no kotlinx-coroutines-play-services dependency needed
     *  just for this one call). */
    private suspend fun fetchLocation(): Location? = suspendCancellableCoroutine { cont ->
        val request = CurrentLocationRequest.Builder()
            .setPriority(Priority.PRIORITY_HIGH_ACCURACY)
            .setDurationMillis(GPS_FIX_TIMEOUT_MS)
            .build()
        val cts = CancellationTokenSource()
        cont.invokeOnCancellation { cts.cancel() }

        try {
            LocationServices.getFusedLocationProviderClient(applicationContext)
                .getCurrentLocation(request, cts.token)
                .addOnSuccessListener { location -> cont.resume(location) }
                .addOnFailureListener { e -> cont.resumeWithException(e) }
        } catch (e: SecurityException) {
            cont.resumeWithException(e)
        }
    }

    /** POSTs to /api/attendance/location-ping. JSON body keys 'lat'/'lng'/
     *  'ts' and the Authorization bearer header are confirmed against
     *  app.py v0.30's actual api_attendance_location_ping() route body —
     *  same token AppPrefs.securePrefs() already stores for Telephony/
     *  punch-in/out, no second store. */
    private fun postLocationPing(token: String, location: Location): Boolean {
        val ts = SimpleDateFormat("yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss", Locale.US).format(Date())
        val body = JSONObject().apply {
            put("lat", location.latitude)
            put("lng", location.longitude)
            put("ts", ts)
        }

        val request = Request.Builder()
            .url("$BASE_URL/api/attendance/location-ping")
            .addHeader("Authorization", "Bearer $token")
            .post(body.toString().toRequestBody("application/json".toMediaType()))
            .build()

        httpClient.newCall(request).execute().use { response ->
            val text = response.body?.string() ?: ""
            if (!response.isSuccessful) {
                throw IOException("HTTP ${response.code}: $text")
            }
            // success:false here just means the server found no open punch
            // for today (cls_db.record_location_ping()'s own no-op case) —
            // NOT an HTTP error, so it's returned as informational only,
            // not thrown/retried.
            return JSONObject(text).optBoolean("success", false)
        }
    }
}

```

```kotlin
package com.asianproperties.clspilot

// Shared.kt v1 (2026-08-01) — extracted while splitting MainActivity into
// two screens (WebView-first main screen + a separate SettingsActivity).
// Both screens need the SAME token/watermark prefs storage — a duplicated
// createEncryptedPrefs() in each file would risk silently drifting into
// two different underlying stores if one copy ever got edited without the
// other. AppPrefs.securePrefs()/syncPrefs() are the single source of truth
// both Activities call. callTypeToString() moved here for the same reason:
// MainActivity's sync path (readCallLogSince) and SettingsActivity's debug
// scan (appendCallLog) both need it.
//
// v2 (2026-08-07) — Option C self-service token-sync redesign. NEW BASE_URL
// + httpClient constants, for the exact same "avoid silent drift between
// copies" reason as everything else in this file: SettingsActivity.kt's new
// "Sync my token" call needed a BASE_URL/OkHttpClient, and PunchActivity.kt
// already had its own PRIVATE copies of both — rather than adding a THIRD
// private copy, they're centralized here. PunchActivity.kt/AttendanceWorker.
// kt are NOT changed to use these — their existing private copies are left
// exactly as they were, untouched, to keep this change scoped to only the
// files actually being edited for this feature.
//
// v3 (2026-08-23) — FCM push wiring. Added KEY_FCM_TOKEN, same additive
// pattern as KEY_LAST_SYNCED_MS/KEY_TOKEN above — FcmService.kt's
// onNewToken() writes it, MainActivity.kt's onCreate() writes it too (the
// token fetched synchronously at launch), and AndroidBridge.getFcmToken()
// reads it back for the WebView's JS.

import android.content.Context
import android.content.SharedPreferences
import android.provider.CallLog
import androidx.security.crypto.EncryptedSharedPreferences
import androidx.security.crypto.MasterKey
import okhttp3.OkHttpClient

const val BASE_URL = "https://crm.asianbuild.in"
val httpClient = OkHttpClient()

object AppPrefs {
    private const val SYNC_PREFS_NAME = "clspilot_sync_prefs"
    private const val SECURE_PREFS_NAME = "clspilot_secure_prefs"
    const val KEY_LAST_SYNCED_MS = "last_synced_timestamp_ms"
    const val KEY_TOKEN = "bearer_token"
    const val KEY_FCM_TOKEN = "fcm_token"

    fun syncPrefs(context: Context): SharedPreferences =
        context.getSharedPreferences(SYNC_PREFS_NAME, Context.MODE_PRIVATE)

    fun securePrefs(context: Context): SharedPreferences {
        val masterKey = MasterKey.Builder(context)
            .setKeyScheme(MasterKey.KeyScheme.AES256_GCM)
            .build()
        return EncryptedSharedPreferences.create(
            context,
            SECURE_PREFS_NAME,
            masterKey,
            EncryptedSharedPreferences.PrefKeyEncryptionScheme.AES256_SIV,
            EncryptedSharedPreferences.PrefValueEncryptionScheme.AES256_GCM
        )
    }
}

fun callTypeToString(type: Int): String = when (type) {
    CallLog.Calls.INCOMING_TYPE -> "INCOMING"
    CallLog.Calls.OUTGOING_TYPE -> "OUTGOING"
    CallLog.Calls.MISSED_TYPE -> "MISSED"
    CallLog.Calls.REJECTED_TYPE -> "REJECTED"
    CallLog.Calls.BLOCKED_TYPE -> "BLOCKED"
    CallLog.Calls.VOICEMAIL_TYPE -> "VOICEMAIL"
    else -> "TYPE_$type"
}
```

## FILE: cls_attendance_photo.py
```python
"""
=============================================================
cls_attendance_photo.py — APX Attendance photo watermarking
=============================================================
Version : 1.0
Author  : Built for Asian Properties / Srikanth

WHAT THIS IS
------------
APX Attendance Chunk A (2026-08-06): server-side compositing of the
punch-in/punch-out selfie. crm/app.py's api_attendance_punch_in/out
routes now call render_punch_photo() instead of saving the uploaded
photo straight to disk.

The client (PunchActivity.kt v3) no longer draws any text watermark
itself — it only resizes/compresses the raw selfie. ALL overlay
drawing (map thumbnail + text, or the plain-text fallback) happens
here, once, so the two never stack on top of each other.

THREE-LAYER FALLBACK ("attendance must never fail over an image
problem" — Srikanth's explicit instruction for this task):
  1. Best case: Google Static Maps pin thumbnail + coordinates/date-
     time text block composited onto the photo.
  2. If ANYTHING in step 1 fails (missing/invalid CLS_MAPS_API_KEY,
     network error, quota, bad response, Pillow decode error) — fall
     back to the OLD plain-text style (numeric Lat/Lng + timestamp,
     no map thumbnail), drawn directly onto the photo via Pillow.
  3. If even step 2 fails (e.g. Pillow itself can't decode the
     upload) — return the original photo bytes completely untouched.
Every layer is wrapped so this module's public function cannot raise.

CLS_MAPS_API_KEY
-----------------
Read from a real OS environment variable at import time — same
"never hardcoded, never in .env" convention as cls_db.py's
CLS_DB_PATH and crm/app.py's CLS_ATTENDANCE_PHOTOS_DIR. No default:
if it's unset, that's logged once at import time and every call
short-circuits straight to the step-2 fallback (no point attempting
a Static Maps request that can only 403).

SCOPE NOTE — coordinates only, not a real street address
----------------------------------------------------------
Srikanth confirmed (2026-08-06) this renders formatted Lat/Lng, not a
reverse-geocoded street address. A real address needs a second,
separate Google Geocoding API call — PunchActivity.kt's own v1
docstring already flagged that as a deferred v1.5 add-on; Chunk A
does not pull it in.

NEW DEPENDENCY: Pillow (not previously installed anywhere in this
codebase) — added to crm/requirements.txt alongside this file.
`requests` was already a project dependency (see CLAUDE.md), no new
dependency there.

WHY THIS ISN'T IN cls_db.py
-----------------------------
This module does no SQLite access at all (record_punch() only ever
stored the photo *filename*, never bytes) — it's image/HTTP work, so
per CLAUDE.md's "All SQLite access stays centralized in cls_db.py"
rule, it belongs in its own small module rather than bloating that
file with non-DB logic.
"""

import io
import logging
import os

import requests

try:
    from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont
    _PIL_AVAILABLE = True
except ImportError:
    _PIL_AVAILABLE = False

log = logging.getLogger("cls_attendance_photo")

CLS_MAPS_API_KEY = os.environ.get("CLS_MAPS_API_KEY")
if not CLS_MAPS_API_KEY:
    log.warning(
        "CLS_MAPS_API_KEY not set — map thumbnail overlay disabled for this "
        "process; every punch photo will use the plain-text fallback style."
    )

STATIC_MAPS_URL = "https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/staticmap"
STATIC_MAPS_TIMEOUT_S = 5          # bounded worst-case delay added to a punch
MAP_THUMB_SIZE_PX = 160            # square thumbnail, bottom-left corner
MAP_ZOOM = 16

TEXT_MARGIN_PX = 14
TEXT_BG_COLOR = (0, 0, 0, 150)     # translucent black band behind text
TEXT_COLOR = (255, 255, 255, 255)

JPEG_SAVE_QUALITY = 85             # composite is drawn on an already-small
                                   # client-resized photo — this is a final
                                   # re-encode pass, not the primary size
                                   # control (that's PunchActivity.kt's job)


def _guarded(label, fn):
    """Runs fn(), logs+returns None on ANY exception instead of raising —
    every step of the map-composite path is wrapped with this so a single
    bad response/timeout/decode error can never propagate up into the
    Flask route and block a punch."""
    try:
        return fn()
    except Exception as e:
        log.warning("cls_attendance_photo: %s failed: %s", label, e)
        return None


def _fetch_map_thumbnail(lat, lng):
    """Static Maps pin-marker thumbnail as PNG bytes, or None on any
    failure. Short, bounded timeout — this must never be the reason a
    punch-in spinner hangs."""
    if not CLS_MAPS_API_KEY:
        return None
    params = {
        "center": f"{lat},{lng}",
        "zoom": MAP_ZOOM,
        "size": f"{MAP_THUMB_SIZE_PX}x{MAP_THUMB_SIZE_PX}",
        "markers": f"color:red|{lat},{lng}",
        "key": CLS_MAPS_API_KEY,
    }
    resp = requests.get(STATIC_MAPS_URL, params=params, timeout=STATIC_MAPS_TIMEOUT_S)
    resp.raise_for_status()
    if not resp.headers.get("Content-Type", "").startswith("image/"):
        # Google returns a 200 with an error image (or JSON, depending on
        # the failure) for some bad-key/quota cases — a non-image
        # Content-Type means treat it as a failure, not a thumbnail.
        raise ValueError(f"Static Maps returned non-image content-type: {resp.headers.get('Content-Type')}")
    return resp.content


def _draw_text_block(draw, xy, lines, font, anchor_right=False, canvas_size=None):
    """Draws `lines` inside a translucent background band, anchored at xy
    (top-left of the block) or right-aligned against canvas_size[0] if
    anchor_right. Shared by both the map-composite text block and the
    plain-text fallback so the two styles share one implementation."""
    line_heights = [draw.textbbox((0, 0), line, font=font)[3] for line in lines]
    line_widths = [draw.textbbox((0, 0), line, font=font)[2] for line in lines]
    block_w = max(line_widths) + 2 * TEXT_MARGIN_PX
    block_h = sum(line_heights) + 2 * TEXT_MARGIN_PX + (len(lines) - 1) * 4

    x0, y0 = xy
    if anchor_right and canvas_size:
        x0 = canvas_size[0] - block_w - TEXT_MARGIN_PX
    draw.rectangle([x0, y0, x0 + block_w, y0 + block_h], fill=TEXT_BG_COLOR)

    cursor_y = y0 + TEXT_MARGIN_PX
    for line, lh in zip(lines, line_heights):
        draw.text((x0 + TEXT_MARGIN_PX, cursor_y), line, font=font, fill=TEXT_COLOR)
        cursor_y += lh + 4


def _load_font():
    """Best-effort truetype font for a slightly nicer look; falls back to
    Pillow's built-in bitmap font (always available, no file dependency)
    if no truetype font can be found on this machine."""
    for candidate in ("arial.ttf", "DejaVuSans.ttf"):
        try:
            return ImageFont.truetype(candidate, 18)
        except Exception:
            continue
    return ImageFont.load_default()


def _composite_with_map(photo_bytes, lat, lng, ts_str):
    """Layer 1 (best case): map thumbnail bottom-left, coordinates/date-
    time text block bottom-right. Returns JPEG bytes, or None if any step
    fails (caller falls back to _plain_text_overlay)."""
    thumb_bytes = _guarded("_fetch_map_thumbnail", lambda: _fetch_map_thumbnail(lat, lng))
    if thumb_bytes is None:
        return None

    base = Image.open(io.BytesIO(photo_bytes)).convert("RGBA")
    thumb = Image.open(io.BytesIO(thumb_bytes)).convert("RGBA")

    overlay = Image.new("RGBA", base.size, (0, 0, 0, 0))
    draw = ImageDraw.Draw(overlay)
    font = _load_font()

    # Map thumbnail, bottom-left, with a small margin, plus a thin white
    # border so it stays visible against a dark photo background.
    thumb_x = TEXT_MARGIN_PX
    thumb_y = base.size[1] - thumb.size[1] - TEXT_MARGIN_PX
    border = Image.new(
        "RGBA", (thumb.size[0] + 4, thumb.size[1] + 4), (255, 255, 255, 220)
    )
    overlay.paste(border, (thumb_x - 2, thumb_y - 2), border)
    overlay.paste(thumb, (thumb_x, thumb_y), thumb)

    lines = [
        "Lat: {:.6f}  Lng: {:.6f}".format(lat, lng),
        ts_str,
    ]
    text_y = base.size[1] - TEXT_MARGIN_PX - 70
    _draw_text_block(draw, (0, text_y), lines, font, anchor_right=True, canvas_size=base.size)

    composited = Image.alpha_composite(base, overlay).convert("RGB")
    out = io.BytesIO()
    composited.save(out, format="JPEG", quality=JPEG_SAVE_QUALITY)
    return out.getvalue()


def _plain_text_overlay(photo_bytes, lat, lng, ts_str):
    """Layer 2 fallback: the OLD client-side watermark style (numeric
    Lat/Lng + timestamp, bottom-left, no map thumbnail) — now drawn
    server-side instead of on the phone. Returns JPEG bytes, or None if
    even this fails (caller falls back to the untouched original)."""
    base = Image.open(io.BytesIO(photo_bytes)).convert("RGBA")
    overlay = Image.new("RGBA", base.size, (0, 0, 0, 0))
    draw = ImageDraw.Draw(overlay)
    font = _load_font()

    lines = [
        "Lat: {:.6f}  Lng: {:.6f}".format(lat, lng),
        ts_str,
    ]
    text_y = base.size[1] - TEXT_MARGIN_PX - 70
    _draw_text_block(draw, (TEXT_MARGIN_PX, text_y), lines, font)

    composited = Image.alpha_composite(base, overlay).convert("RGB")
    out = io.BytesIO()
    composited.save(out, format="JPEG", quality=JPEG_SAVE_QUALITY)
    return out.getvalue()


def render_punch_photo(photo_bytes, lat, lng, ts_str):
    """
    Public entry point — called by crm/app.py's punch-in/punch-out routes
    in place of the old `uploaded.save(path)`.

    photo_bytes : raw JPEG bytes as uploaded by PunchActivity.kt (already
                  resized/compressed client-side — this function does not
                  resize, only overlays).
    lat, lng    : floats, already validated by _parse_punch_request().
    ts_str      : the same 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' string app.py computed
                  for this punch.

    Returns JPEG bytes to write to disk. NEVER raises — worst case
    (Pillow missing, or every layer fails) returns photo_bytes unchanged,
    so a photo/map problem can never fail the punch itself.
    """
    if not _PIL_AVAILABLE:
        log.warning("cls_attendance_photo: Pillow not installed — saving photo unmodified.")
        return photo_bytes

    result = _guarded("_composite_with_map", lambda: _composite_with_map(photo_bytes, lat, lng, ts_str))
    if result is not None:
        return result

    result = _guarded("_plain_text_overlay", lambda: _plain_text_overlay(photo_bytes, lat, lng, ts_str))
    if result is not None:
        return result

    log.warning("cls_attendance_photo: all overlay layers failed — saving original photo unmodified.")
    return photo_bytes

```

## FILE: crm/templates/_leads_list_actionbar.html
```html
{# _leads_list_actionbar.html (v0.8) — bottom icon bar for the leads
   list page, replacing the old inline top filter form. Filter/Search
   link through to dedicated screens, carrying every currently-active
   filter forward as query params so nothing gets silently reset.
   Fields stays an in-place popover (unchanged mechanism from before —
   just relocated here from the old top bar). Reuses the same
   .action-bar/.action-btn classes as the dashboard tab bar and
   lead_detail's action bar.

   The Fields popover is a SIBLING of its trigger button, not nested
   inside it — nesting interactive content (checkboxes) inside a
   <button> is invalid HTML and would make a checkbox click also
   bubble up as a button click, toggling the popover shut the instant
   you tried to check something.

   v0.8 (2026-08-04) — Pipeline Stage carry-forward query param on both
   breadcrumb links changed from stage=filters.stage to
   stages=filters.stages (Jinja/Flask url_for repeats a param once per
   list item, so this correctly emits one stages=... per selected
   value) — matches leads_filter.html's radio->checkbox conversion
   (app.py v0.33 / cls_db.py v2.44). #}
<div class="action-bar">
  <a class="action-btn" href="{{ url_for('leads_filter_screen', q=filters.q, stages=filters.stages, project=filters.project, owner=filters.owner, date_from=filters.date_from, date_to=filters.date_to, sort_by=filters.sort_by, stage_reason=filters.stage_reason, campaign=filters.campaign, source=filters.source, sub_source=filters.sub_source, budget=filters.budget, configuration=filters.configuration, property_type=filters.property_type, facing=filters.facing) }}" title="Filter">
    <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"><path d="M4 6h16M7 12h10M10 18h4"/></svg>
    Filter
  </a>
  <a class="action-btn" href="{{ url_for('leads_search_screen', stages=filters.stages, project=filters.project, owner=filters.owner, date_from=filters.date_from, date_to=filters.date_to, sort_by=filters.sort_by, stage_reason=filters.stage_reason, campaign=filters.campaign, source=filters.source, sub_source=filters.sub_source, budget=filters.budget, configuration=filters.configuration, property_type=filters.property_type, facing=filters.facing) }}" title="Search">
    <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"><circle cx="11" cy="11" r="7"/><line x1="21" y1="21" x2="16.65" y2="16.65"/></svg>
    Search
  </a>
  <button type="button" class="action-btn" id="fieldsBtn" onclick="toggleFieldsPopover(this)" title="Fields">
    <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"><rect x="3" y="4" width="18" height="4"/><rect x="3" y="10" width="18" height="4"/><rect x="3" y="16" width="10" height="4"/></svg>
    Fields
  </button>

  <div id="fieldsPopover" class="fields-popover">
    <div style="font-size:12px; color:var(--ink-soft); text-transform:uppercase; letter-spacing:0.03em; margin-bottom:8px;">Show columns</div>
    {% for f in all_fields %}
    <label style="display:flex; align-items:center; gap:8px; padding:5px 0; font-size:14px; cursor:pointer;">
      <input type="checkbox" name="fields" value="{{ f }}" {% if f in active_fields %}checked{% endif %} onchange="submitFieldsChange()">
      {{ f|capitalize }}
    </label>
    {% endfor %}
  </div>
</div>

<script>
// Fixes the popover rendering off-screen on narrow phones: instead of
// relying purely on CSS `right: 0` relative to wherever the button
// happens to land, compute its position explicitly from the button's
// actual location and clamp it to stay within the viewport. Anchored
// ABOVE the button (bottom bar sits at the screen edge, so the
// popover has nowhere to go but up).
function toggleFieldsPopover(btn){
  var pop = document.getElementById('fieldsPopover');
  var isOpen = pop.classList.contains('open');
  if (isOpen) {
    pop.classList.remove('open');
    return;
  }
  pop.classList.add('open');
  pop.style.position = 'fixed';
  var margin = 12;
  var btnRect = btn.getBoundingClientRect();
  var popWidth = pop.offsetWidth || 200;
  var viewportWidth = window.innerWidth;

  var left = btnRect.right - popWidth;
  if (left < margin) left = margin;
  if (left + popWidth > viewportWidth - margin) left = viewportWidth - popWidth - margin;

  pop.style.left = left + 'px';
  pop.style.right = 'auto';
  pop.style.bottom = (window.innerHeight - btnRect.top + 6) + 'px';
  pop.style.top = 'auto';
}

document.addEventListener('click', function(e){
  var pop = document.getElementById('fieldsPopover');
  var btn = document.getElementById('fieldsBtn');
  if (pop && pop.classList.contains('open') && !pop.contains(e.target) && e.target !== btn && !btn.contains(e.target)) {
    pop.classList.remove('open');
  }
});

// Re-submits the current URL with the updated `fields` selection the
// moment a checkbox is toggled — same "instant apply" feel; Filter/
// Search still need their own explicit submit since those are full
// screens, but Fields is a lightweight in-place toggle.
function submitFieldsChange(){
  var params = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search);
  params.set('fields_submitted', '1');
  params.delete('fields');
  document.querySelectorAll('#fieldsPopover input[type=checkbox]:checked').forEach(function(cb){
    params.append('fields', cb.value);
  });
  window.location.search = params.toString();
}
</script>

```

```html
{# _report_date_picker.html (v0.7) — shared date-range picker, included
   by both report_view.html and report_view_charts.html so the markup/
   logic for "which range is this report showing" lives in exactly one
   place. Expects `report` (from cls_reports.build_report()) in context
   — both templates' routes already pass this; `quick_select_links` is
   no longer read here (see below).

   report.is_live reports (Pipeline Funnel Snapshot, Lead Score
   Distribution, Owner-wise Workload) get a small "Live snapshot" note
   instead of a picker — Requirement 1's explicit exemption list,
   unchanged.

   v0.7 (July 2026, Task 1) — the old row of 4 quick-link buttons
   (Today/This Week/This Month/Last 30 Days) is replaced with an
   11-option <select> dropdown (Today / Yesterday / Last 7 days /
   Last 14 days / Last 30 days / This week / Last week / This month /
   Last month / Maximum / Custom), same option set and same auto-submit-
   unless-Custom JS pattern as leads_filter.html's onDatePresetChange().
   Selecting anything except "Custom" submits immediately; "Custom"
   reveals the From/To inputs and still requires the Apply button.
   Driven entirely by cls_reports.build_report()'s new
   report.date_preset / report.date_preset_order / report.date_preset_labels
   keys — no new template context needed from app.py's routes, so
   app.py itself is untouched by this change. #}
{% if report.is_live %}
<div class="card no-print" style="margin-top:14px; background:#F0F4FF; border-color:#C9D6F5;">
  <p style="font-size:12px; color:var(--ink-soft); margin:0;">
    Live snapshot (as of {{ now }}) — not scoped to a date range.
  </p>
</div>
{% else %}
<form method="get" action="{{ url_for('report_view', report_id=report.id) }}"
      id="reportDateForm" class="no-print"
      style="margin-top:14px; display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:8px; align-items:center;">
  <select name="preset" id="reportDatePresetSelect" onchange="onReportDatePresetChange(this)"
          style="height:34px; font-size:13px; padding:4px 8px;">
    <option value="" {% if not report.date_preset %}selected{% endif %}>— Select —</option>
    {% for key in report.date_preset_order %}
    <option value="{{ key }}" {% if report.date_preset == key %}selected{% endif %}>{{ report.date_preset_labels[key] }}</option>
    {% endfor %}
  </select>
  <div id="customReportDateFields"
       style="display:{{ 'flex' if report.date_preset == 'custom' else 'none' }}; gap:6px; align-items:center;">
    <input type="date" name="from" value="{{ report.date_from }}" style="height:34px; font-size:13px; padding:4px 8px;" aria-label="From date">
    <span style="font-size:13px; color:var(--ink-soft);">to</span>
    <input type="date" name="to" value="{{ report.date_to }}" style="height:34px; font-size:13px; padding:4px 8px;" aria-label="To date">
  </div>
  <button type="submit" class="btn" style="padding:5px 14px; font-size:13px;">Apply</button>
</form>
<script>
function onReportDatePresetChange(sel){
  var customBox = document.getElementById('customReportDateFields');
  if (sel.value === 'custom') {
    customBox.style.display = 'flex';
    return;
  }
  customBox.style.display = 'none';
  if (sel.value !== '') {
    sel.form.submit();
  }
}
</script>
{% endif %}
```
