```html
  </form>
</div>

<script>
function toggleOwnerField() {
  var role = document.getElementById('roleSelect').value;
  var wrap = document.getElementById('ownerFieldWrap');
  var field = document.getElementById('ownerField');
  var hint = document.getElementById('ownerFieldHint');
  var needsOwner = (role === 'salesperson' || role === 'manager');
  wrap.style.display = needsOwner ? 'block' : 'none';
  field.required = needsOwner;
  if (role === 'manager') {
    hint.textContent = "This links the manager to their OWN leads (they still see everyone's). " +
      "Open Sell.do, find one of their leads, and copy the exact \"Attended By\" text.";
  } else {
    hint.textContent = "This person only sees their own leads, matched by this exact text. " +
      "Open Sell.do, find one of their leads, and copy the exact \"Attended By\" text.";
  }
}
document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', toggleOwnerField);
</script>
{% endblock %}

```


## FILE: crm/templates/settings_users.html
```html
{# settings_users.html (v0.11) — admin Settings > Team. Lists every CRM
   login with an activate/deactivate toggle. Reuses users.active, already
   enforced by verify_login()/get_user_by_id() since v0.1 — this screen is
   new UI on an existing flag, not a new access-control mechanism.

   v0.9.4 — own row no longer shows a Deactivate button (backend already
   refused this in cls_db.set_user_active(); this just stops offering it).

   v0.11 — NEW "View as" button, just to the left of Deactivate, for
   every row that is: not the current admin, not another admin, and
   active. Posts to impersonate_start() (app.py) — a secondary,
   diagnostic action, so it's styled as a plain .btn, not .btn-primary.

   v0.12 — NEW "+ Add User" link at the top, pointing at
   settings_user_new() (app.py) — the first in-app way to create a CRM
   login.

   v0.28 — NEW per-row "Attendance project" dropdown (APX Attendance
   geofencing, cls_db.py v2.38's users.assigned_project column). A
   small addition to this EXISTING screen rather than a new "edit
   user" screen — deliberately, per the v0.9 spec's "fewer templates"
   call. Posts to its own small route (settings_user_assign_project),
   separate from the activate/deactivate form so saving one can never
   accidentally affect the other. #}
{% extends "base.html" %}
{% block title %}Team{% endblock %}

{% block content %}
<a href="{{ url_for('settings_home') }}" style="font-size:14px;">← Back to Settings</a>
<div style="display:flex; justify-content:space-between; align-items:center; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:10px;">
  <h2 style="margin-top:10px;">Team</h2>
  <a href="{{ url_for('settings_user_new') }}" class="btn btn-primary" style="margin-top:10px;">+ Add User</a>
</div>
<p style="font-size:13px; color:var(--ink-soft); max-width:600px; margin-top:-6px;">
  Activate or deactivate a login. Deactivating someone blocks their next login/request
  immediately — it does not delete their account, name, or history anywhere in the CRM.
</p>

<div style="display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:12px; margin-top:16px;">
  {% for u in users %}
  <div class="card">
    <div style="display:flex; justify-content:space-between; align-items:center; gap:10px; flex-wrap:wrap;">
      <div>
        <strong style="font-size:15px;">{{ u.full_name or '(no name)' }}</strong>
        {# v0.9.5 — three-tier badge: admin (blue) / manager (violet) /
           salesperson (gray). Cosmetic only — role behaviour is enforced
           in app.py + cls_db.can_view_all_leads(), never from this colour. #}
        <span class="badge" style="background:{{ 'var(--blue)' if u.role == 'admin' else ('#7C5CBF' if u.role == 'manager' else 'var(--ink-soft)') }}; margin-left:6px;">
          {{ u.role or 'salesperson' }}
        </span>
        {% if not u.active %}
        <span class="badge" style="background:var(--red); margin-left:6px;">Inactive</span>
        {% endif %}
        <div style="font-size:13px; color:var(--ink-soft); margin-top:4px;">{{ u.email }}</div>
        <div style="font-size:12px; color:var(--ink-soft); margin-top:2px;">
          Last login: {{ u.last_login_at|ampm if u.last_login_at else 'Never' }}
        </div>
      </div>
      {% if u.user_id == current_user.user_id %}
      {# v0.9.4 — this row is the logged-in admin themself. cls_db.set_user_active()
         already refuses self-deactivation server-side (can't lock yourself out with
         no other admin able to undo it) — this just hides the button so it's never
         offered in the first place instead of showing after a failed click. #}
      <span style="font-size:13px; color:var(--ink-soft); padding:5px 14px;">This is you</span>
      {% else %}
      <div style="display:flex; gap:8px; align-items:center;">
        {% if u.role != 'admin' and u.active %}
        <form method="post" action="{{ url_for('impersonate_start', user_id=u.user_id) }}"
              onsubmit="return confirm('View the CRM as {{ u.full_name or u.email }}? Any actions you take will be recorded as BOTH you and them.');">
          <button type="submit" class="btn" style="padding:5px 14px; font-size:13px;">View as</button>
        </form>
        {% endif %}
        <form method="post" action="{{ url_for('settings_user_toggle', user_id=u.user_id) }}"
              {% if u.active %}onsubmit="return confirm('Deactivate {{ u.full_name or u.email }}? They will be signed out on their next request.');"{% endif %}>
          <input type="hidden" name="active" value="{{ '0' if u.active else '1' }}">
          {% if u.active %}
          <button type="submit" class="btn" style="color:var(--red); border-color:#F3C9C9; padding:5px 14px; font-size:13px;">Deactivate</button>
          {% else %}
          <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary" style="padding:5px 14px; font-size:13px;">Activate</button>
          {% endif %}
        </form>
      </div>
      {% endif %}
    </div>
    {# v0.28 — Attendance project assignment (geofencing). Separate
       small form so saving it can never affect activate/deactivate. #}
    <form method="post" action="{{ url_for('settings_user_assign_project', user_id=u.user_id) }}"
          style="display:flex; align-items:center; gap:8px; margin-top:10px; padding-top:10px; border-top:1px solid var(--line);">
      <label style="font-size:12px; color:var(--ink-soft); white-space:nowrap;">Attendance project</label>
      <select name="assigned_project" style="max-width:220px;">
        <option value="">(not assigned)</option>
        {% for p in projects %}
        <option value="{{ p }}" {% if u.assigned_project == p %}selected{% endif %}>{{ p }}</option>
        {% endfor %}
      </select>
      <button type="submit" class="btn" style="padding:5px 14px; font-size:13px;">Save</button>
    </form>
  </div>
  {% endfor %}
</div>

{% if not users %}
<div class="card empty-state">
  <p>No users found.</p>
</div>
{% endif %}
{% endblock %}

```


## FILE: crm/templates/settings_whatsapp.html
```html
{# settings_whatsapp.html (v0.9.1) — admin CRUD for WhatsApp templates.
   One template per project (project is the unique title). Saving an
   existing project overwrites it; a new project name adds one. #}
{% extends "base.html" %}
{% block title %}WhatsApp Templates{% endblock %}

{% block content %}
<a href="{{ url_for('settings_home') }}" style="font-size:14px;">← Back to Settings</a>
<h2 style="margin-top:10px;">WhatsApp Templates</h2>
<p style="font-size:13px; color:var(--ink-soft); max-width:600px; margin-top:-6px;">
  One message per project. When a salesperson taps WhatsApp on a lead, they pick a
  project here and it opens WhatsApp pre-filled with this message.
  Use <code>{name}</code> for the lead's name and <code>{project}</code> for the project name —
  they'll be filled in automatically.
</p>

{# ── Add / edit form ── #}
<div class="card" style="margin-top:16px;">
  <h3 style="margin-top:0; font-size:16px;">Add or update a template</h3>
  <form method="post" action="{{ url_for('whatsapp_template_save') }}">
    <div class="field-label">Project (template title) *</div>
    <input list="projectList" type="text" name="project" required placeholder="e.g. Naishka" style="width:100%; margin-bottom:14px;">
    <datalist id="projectList">
      {% for p in projects %}<option value="{{ p }}">{% endfor %}
    </datalist>

    <div class="field-label">Message *</div>
    <textarea name="message_body" required placeholder="Hi {name}, thank you for your interest in {project}. Here are the details..."
              style="width:100%; min-height:120px; padding:10px 12px; border:1.5px solid var(--line); border-radius:8px; font-family:inherit; font-size:14px; resize:vertical;"></textarea>

    <div style="margin-top:12px;">
      <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">Save template</button>
    </div>
  </form>
</div>

{# ── Existing templates ── #}
<h3 style="margin-top:24px; font-size:16px;">Existing templates ({{ templates|length }})</h3>
{% if templates %}
<div style="display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:12px;">
  {% for t in templates %}
  <div class="card">
    <div style="display:flex; justify-content:space-between; align-items:center; gap:10px; flex-wrap:wrap;">
      <strong style="font-size:15px;">{{ t.project }}</strong>
      <form method="post" action="{{ url_for('whatsapp_template_delete', template_id=t.template_id) }}"
            onsubmit="return confirm('Delete the WhatsApp template for {{ t.project }}? This cannot be undone.');">
        <button type="submit" class="btn" style="color:var(--red); border-color:#F3C9C9; padding:5px 12px; font-size:13px;">Delete</button>
      </form>
    </div>
    <div style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-size:14px; color:var(--ink); margin-top:8px; background:var(--paper); padding:10px 12px; border-radius:8px;">{{ t.message_body }}</div>
    <div style="font-size:12px; color:var(--ink-soft); margin-top:6px;">
      To edit: retype this project name above with the new message and save — it overwrites this one.
    </div>
  </div>
  {% endfor %}
</div>
{% else %}
<div class="card empty-state">
  <p>No templates yet. Add one above — start with your most-used project.</p>
</div>
{% endif %}
{% endblock %}

```

## FILE: crm/templates/webhook_test_leads.html
```html
{# webhook_test_leads.html (v1.0) — Meta App Review screencast support.
   Admin-only viewer for cls_db.get_webhook_test_leads() (webhook_test_leads
   table, cls_db.py v2.56). Isolated from the real leads table — this exists
   purely so a reviewer's fake test payload can be visually confirmed on
   screen during Meta's App Review screencast. Newest first, LIMIT 50,
   no pagination — plain table, same style as settings_bulk_jobs.html. #}
{% extends "base.html" %}
{% block title %}Webhook Test Leads{% endblock %}

{% block content %}
<h2 style="margin-top:10px; margin-bottom:6px;">Meta Webhook Test Leads</h2>
<p style="color:var(--ink-soft); font-size:13px; margin-bottom:14px;">
  Isolated log of payloads received at /webhooks/meta-leadgen. For App
  Review verification only — never written to the real leads table.
</p>

{% if rows %}
<div class="report-table-wrap" style="overflow-x:auto;">
  <table class="report-table" style="width:100%; border-collapse:collapse;">
    <thead>
      <tr>
        <th style="text-align:left; padding:8px 10px; border-bottom:1px solid var(--line); font-size:12px; color:var(--ink-soft); text-transform:uppercase;">Received</th>
        <th style="text-align:left; padding:8px 10px; border-bottom:1px solid var(--line); font-size:12px; color:var(--ink-soft); text-transform:uppercase;">Leadgen ID</th>
        <th style="text-align:left; padding:8px 10px; border-bottom:1px solid var(--line); font-size:12px; color:var(--ink-soft); text-transform:uppercase;">Form ID</th>
        <th style="text-align:left; padding:8px 10px; border-bottom:1px solid var(--line); font-size:12px; color:var(--ink-soft); text-transform:uppercase;">Page ID</th>
        <th style="text-align:left; padding:8px 10px; border-bottom:1px solid var(--line); font-size:12px; color:var(--ink-soft); text-transform:uppercase;">Raw Payload</th>
      </tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
      {% for row in rows %}
      <tr>
        <td style="padding:8px 10px; border-bottom:1px solid var(--line); font-size:13px; white-space:nowrap; vertical-align:top;">{{ row.received_at }}</td>
        <td style="padding:8px 10px; border-bottom:1px solid var(--line); font-size:13px; vertical-align:top;">{{ row.leadgen_id or '—' }}</td>
        <td style="padding:8px 10px; border-bottom:1px solid var(--line); font-size:13px; vertical-align:top;">{{ row.form_id or '—' }}</td>
        <td style="padding:8px 10px; border-bottom:1px solid var(--line); font-size:13px; vertical-align:top;">{{ row.page_id or '—' }}</td>
        <td style="padding:8px 10px; border-bottom:1px solid var(--line); font-size:13px;">
          <pre style="white-space:pre-wrap; word-break:break-word; margin:0; font-size:12px; background:var(--gray); padding:8px; border-radius:6px;">{{ row.raw_payload }}</pre>
        </td>
      </tr>
      {% endfor %}
    </tbody>
  </table>
</div>
{% else %}
<div class="card empty-state">
  <p>No webhook test leads received yet.</p>
</div>
{% endif %}
{% endblock %}
```

```html
{# whatsapp_picker.html (v0.9.7) — the screen the lead-page WhatsApp
   button opens.

   v0.9.7 — Debug box removed. v0.9.6's whatsapp://send link confirmed
   working by Srikanth on the real device/team flow (2026-08-27) — the
   emoji-corruption complaint is CLOSED. The temporary "Debug: link
   comparison" box from v0.9.5/v0.9.6 served its purpose (isolating
   that wa.me's own intermediate webpage — not this codebase — was
   re-serializing and corrupting astral-plane/emoji characters before
   handoff) and is now stripped. No other behavior changed from v0.9.6.

   v0.9.6 — Root cause found. Srikanth confirmed via controlled testing
   that the generated URL text was byte-perfect (verified by decoding
   it character-by-character — zero corruption), and that the template
   renders correctly whenever WhatsApp is reached WITHOUT passing
   through wa.me's own "Chat on WhatsApp with +91..." webpage. The real
   button-tap flow (this page -> https://wa.me/... -> that intermediate
   Meta-hosted webpage -> "Open with" chooser -> real chat) showed "�"
   ALREADY on that intermediate page, and that same corrupted text
   landed in the actual chat compose box — i.e. wa.me's page was
   re-serializing (and mangling emoji in) the text before handing off
   to WhatsApp. That's a bug on Meta's servers, not this codebase, but
   it's avoidable: WhatsApp also accepts a direct app-level link,
   whatsapp://send?phone=..&text=.., which opens WhatsApp (or the
   chooser between 2 installed WhatsApp apps) WITHOUT ever visiting
   wa.me's webpage. sendBtn now targets whatsapp:// instead of
   https://wa.me/ — same direct client-side <a href> tap mechanism as
   before, so it didn't reintroduce the v0.9.4 gesture-loss bug (that
   one was specifically about a multi-hop SERVER redirect chain, not
   about the target scheme of a single client tap).

   v0.9.5 — TEMPORARY diagnostic addition (now removed in v0.9.7).
   Added a debug box showing the raw generated link(s) with a Copy
   button, to capture the exact on-device URL for offline byte-level
   inspection during the investigation above.

   v0.9.4 — PWA deep-link fix. Send used to be a <form method=post>
   submit that the server 302-redirected to https://wa.me/..., which
   itself redirects to whatsapp://... — in an installed/standalone PWA
   that redirect chain loses user-gesture status, so the OS blocks the
   whatsapp:// custom scheme (net::ERR_UNKNOWN_URL_SCHEME). Send is now
   a real <a href="...">, kept in sync with the project/message pickers
   via JS (href recomputed on every change/input event, same trigger
   refreshSendState() already used). The disabled state (no message
   yet) is emulated with pointer-events/tabindex toggling, since
   anchors have no native `disabled`. On click, the same activity-log
   POST still fires — via fetch(..., {keepalive:true}), not awaited, no
   preventDefault — so the anchor's own navigation proceeds
   un-intercepted. See app.py's whatsapp_send(), which returns 204
   instead of redirecting since the browser navigates via the anchor's
   own href independently.

   v0.9.2 — items 2/3 redesign. The old screen listed every project's
   template as a full card (message text visible + scrollable) — with
   only 2 templates each card already ate half the screen on mobile.
   Replaced with a 2-field flow: (1) a project dropdown, (2) one
   textarea that fills with that project's message on selection, is
   editable in place, and scrolls if long. Send appears right after
   the textarea and opens WhatsApp with whatever is CURRENTLY in the
   textarea (edited or not). No app.py/cls_db.py change — same
   `templates` data the route already rendered per-lead in v0.9.1,
   just presented one at a time instead of all at once.

   v0.9.3 (Task 2.2) — Send used to be client-side only (window.open,
   no server round-trip, nothing logged). Now a real <form
   method="post"> to the new /leads/<cls_id>/whatsapp/send route —
   hidden wa_url/project/message fields are filled by JS right before
   submit (they depend on whatever's currently selected/edited), the
   route logs an activity_log row then 302-redirects into WhatsApp.
   Same end-user experience (tap Send, WhatsApp opens with the message
   pre-filled), just with an audit trail now. #}
{% extends "base.html" %}
{% block title %}Send WhatsApp{% endblock %}

{% block content %}
<a href="{{ url_for('lead_detail', cls_id=lead.cls_id) }}" style="font-size:14px;">← Back to lead</a>
<h2 style="margin-top:10px; margin-bottom:4px;">Send WhatsApp</h2>
<p style="font-size:13px; color:var(--ink-soft); margin-top:0;">
  To <strong>{{ lead.full_name or '(no name)' }}</strong> · {{ lead.phone_raw or lead.phone_norm }}
</p>

{% if templates %}
<div class="card" style="margin-top:8px;">
  <div class="field-label">1. Project</div>
  <select id="waProject" style="width:100%; padding:9px 10px; border:1.5px solid var(--line); border-radius:8px; font-family:inherit; font-size:14px; margin-bottom:16px;">
    <option value="">Select a project…</option>
    {% for t in templates %}
    <option value="{{ t.template_id }}">{{ t.project }}</option>
    {% endfor %}
  </select>

  <div class="field-label">2. Message <span style="color:var(--ink-soft); font-weight:400;">(edit if needed)</span></div>
  <textarea id="waMessage" placeholder="Pick a project above to load its message here."
            style="width:100%; min-height:160px; max-height:320px; padding:10px 12px; border:1.5px solid var(--line); border-radius:8px; font-family:inherit; font-size:14px; resize:vertical; overflow:auto; background:var(--paper);"></textarea>

  <a id="waSendBtn" class="btn btn-primary" href="#" tabindex="-1" aria-disabled="true"
     style="display:block; width:100%; margin-top:14px; padding:10px; font-size:15px; text-align:center; box-sizing:border-box; opacity:0.5; pointer-events:none;">
    Open WhatsApp →
  </a>
</div>

<script>
(function () {
  var TEMPLATES = {{ templates|tojson }};
  var PHONE = {{ phone_e164|tojson }};
  var LOG_URL = {{ url_for('whatsapp_send', cls_id=lead.cls_id)|tojson }};

  var projectSel = document.getElementById('waProject');
  var msgBox = document.getElementById('waMessage');
  var sendBtn = document.getElementById('waSendBtn');

  function byId(id) {
    for (var i = 0; i < TEMPLATES.length; i++) {
      if (String(TEMPLATES[i].template_id) === String(id)) return TEMPLATES[i];
    }
    return null;
  }

  function refreshSendState() {
    var enabled = msgBox.value.trim().length > 0;
    if (enabled) {
      // v0.9.6 — whatsapp:// direct link, bypassing wa.me's
      // intermediate webpage (confirmed source of emoji corruption —
      // see changelog above). Confirmed working 2026-08-27.
      sendBtn.href = 'whatsapp://send?phone=' + PHONE + '&text=' + encodeURIComponent(msgBox.value);
      sendBtn.removeAttribute('tabindex');
      sendBtn.setAttribute('aria-disabled', 'false');
      sendBtn.style.opacity = '1';
      sendBtn.style.pointerEvents = 'auto';
    } else {
      sendBtn.href = '#';
      sendBtn.setAttribute('tabindex', '-1');
      sendBtn.setAttribute('aria-disabled', 'true');
      sendBtn.style.opacity = '0.5';
      sendBtn.style.pointerEvents = 'none';
    }
  }

  projectSel.addEventListener('change', function () {
    var t = byId(projectSel.value);
    msgBox.value = t ? t.message : '';
    refreshSendState();
  });

  msgBox.addEventListener('input', refreshSendState);

  sendBtn.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
    if (sendBtn.getAttribute('aria-disabled') === 'true') { e.preventDefault(); return; }
    var t = byId(projectSel.value);
    var fd = new FormData();
    fd.append('wa_url', sendBtn.href);
    fd.append('project', t ? t.project : '');
    fd.append('message', msgBox.value);
    // Fire-and-forget: not awaited, no preventDefault — the anchor's
    // own top-level navigation to whatsapp:// must proceed
    // un-intercepted so the OS still treats it as a user gesture.
    fetch(LOG_URL, { method: 'POST', body: fd, keepalive: true });
  });
})();
</script>
{% else %}
<div class="card empty-state">
  <p><strong>No WhatsApp templates set up yet.</strong></p>
  {% if current_user.role == 'admin' %}
  <p>Add one under <a href="{{ url_for('whatsapp_templates_admin') }}">Settings → WhatsApp Templates</a>.</p>
  {% else %}
  <p>Ask your admin to add project templates under Settings.</p>
  {% endif %}
</div>
{% endif %}
{% endblock %}

```

<!-- modified: 15d ago | last git commit: 2026-08-17 | in a .bat wrapper: yes | imported elsewhere: no -->
```python
"""
=============================================================
cls_monday_weekly_report.py  —  CLS Monday Morning Weekly Report
=============================================================
Version : 1.1
Author  : Built for Asian Properties / Srikanth

CHANGELOG
---------
v1.1 (2026-08-17) — Per-salesperson breakdown. Appends a "Per
  Salesperson" section to the Telegram message, sourced from the new
  cls_db.get_monday_weekly_report_by_owner() (cls_db.py v2.61). Owners
  with all-zero activity for the week are skipped from the list (not
  every inactive user printed every week); if literally every owner is
  zero, one fallback line is shown instead of an empty section — same
  "never skip sending silently" posture as the v1.0 zero-visits case.
  build_message() split into build_company_section()/
  build_owner_section() for locality; main()'s send/log/write_job_
  result plumbing is unchanged.
v1.0 (2026-08-17) — Initial version. Automated 5-metric weekly summary
  (leads generated, site visits scheduled, site visits conducted,
  bookings weekday/weekend) for the most recently completed Mon-Sun
  week, sent via Telegram every Monday morning. Ops-only script, same
  status as cls_weekend_visits_report.py (not "Job E" in
  job_results.txt — see write_job_result() call below) — it doesn't
  participate in the A-B-C-D flag-gated hand-off chain, it just reads
  cls_db.get_monday_weekly_report_stats() (cls_db.py v2.60) on its own
  Monday-morning Task Scheduler trigger.

WHAT THIS SCRIPT DOES
----------------------
Every Monday morning (Task Scheduler, see run_cls_monday_weekly_
report.bat), computes the most recently completed Mon-Sun week and
sends Srikanth a Telegram message (HTML parse_mode, same as
cls_watchdog.py) with the 5 company-wide headline numbers, a computed
Total Bookings line, and a per-salesperson breakdown. Falls back to a
Brevo email if Telegram is unavailable — same primary/fallback pattern
cls_watchdog.py's run() uses, reusing its load_env()/send_telegram()/
send_brevo_alert() rather than duplicating that logic.

USAGE
-----
  python cls_monday_weekly_report.py             # normal run
  python cls_monday_weekly_report.py --selftest  # sends a fixed test
                                                    # message, no DB query
"""

import os
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

BASE_DIR = r"D:\CLS"
sys.path.insert(0, BASE_DIR)
import cls_db
import cls_watchdog   # reuse load_env()/send_telegram()/send_brevo_alert() —
                       # its own run logic lives behind __main__, so importing
                       # it here has no side effects.

LOG_FILE = os.path.join(BASE_DIR, "cls_monday_weekly_report_log.txt")

# pythonw.exe has no console — sys.stdout is None. Guard before reconfiguring.
if sys.stdout is not None:
    sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# LOGGING
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def log(message, level="INFO"):
    ts = datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
    entry = f"[{ts}] [{level}] {message}"
    try:
        if sys.stdout is not None:
            print(entry)
    except Exception:
        pass
    try:
        os.makedirs(BASE_DIR, exist_ok=True)
        with open(LOG_FILE, "a", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
            f.write(entry + "\n")
    except Exception:
        pass


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# MESSAGE BUILDING
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def _last_week_range():
    """
    The most recently completed Mon-Sun week, relative to today —
    robust to manual re-runs on any day of the week, not just Monday.
    """
    today = datetime.now().date()
    this_monday = today - timedelta(days=today.weekday())
    week_end = this_monday - timedelta(days=1)      # last Sunday
    week_start = week_end - timedelta(days=6)        # Monday before that
    return week_start, week_end


def build_company_section(stats, week_start, week_end):
    """
    Builds the company-wide totals portion of the HTML-formatted
    Telegram message. Returns a list of lines.
    """
    date_range = f"{week_start.strftime('%a, %b %d')} – {week_end.strftime('%a, %b %d')}"

    return [
        f"📊 <b>Weekly Report — {date_range}</b>",
        "",
        f"🧲 Leads Generated: <b>{stats['leads_generated']}</b>",
        f"🗓️ Site Visits Scheduled: <b>{stats['site_visits_scheduled']}</b>",
        f"✅ Site Visits Conducted: <b>{stats['site_visits_conducted']}</b>",
        f"💼 Bookings (Weekdays): <b>{stats['bookings_weekday']}</b>",
        f"🏡 Bookings (Weekend): <b>{stats['bookings_weekend']}</b>",
        "",
        f"Total Bookings: <b>{stats['bookings_total']}</b>",
    ]


def build_owner_section(owner_rows):
    """
    Builds the per-salesperson breakdown portion of the HTML-formatted
    Telegram message. Returns a list of lines. Owners with all-zero
    activity for the week are skipped; if every owner is zero, one
    fallback line is shown instead of an empty section — same "never
    skip sending silently" posture as the company section's zero case.
    """
    active_rows = [
        r for r in owner_rows
        if r["leads_generated"] or r["site_visits_scheduled"]
        or r["site_visits_conducted"] or r["bookings_total"]
    ]

    lines = ["", "👥 <b>Per Salesperson</b>"]
    if not active_rows:
        lines.append("No salesperson activity this week.")
        return lines

    for r in active_rows:
        lines.append(
            f"👤 {r['owner']} — Leads: {r['leads_generated']} | "
            f"Scheduled: {r['site_visits_scheduled']} | "
            f"Conducted: {r['site_visits_conducted']} | "
            f"Bookings: {r['bookings_total']}"
        )

    return lines


def build_message(stats, owner_rows, week_start, week_end):
    """Builds the full HTML-formatted Telegram message. Returns a string."""
    lines = build_company_section(stats, week_start, week_end)
    lines += build_owner_section(owner_rows)
    return "\n".join(lines)


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# MAIN
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def main():
    log("=" * 55)
    log("CLS MONDAY WEEKLY REPORT — START")
    log("=" * 55)

    week_start, week_end = _last_week_range()
    stats = cls_db.get_monday_weekly_report_stats(week_start.isoformat(), week_end.isoformat())
    owner_rows = cls_db.get_monday_weekly_report_by_owner(week_start.isoformat(), week_end.isoformat())
    message = build_message(stats, owner_rows, week_start, week_end)
    log(f"Week {week_start.isoformat()} - {week_end.isoformat()}: "
        f"leads={stats['leads_generated']}, "
        f"visits_scheduled={stats['site_visits_scheduled']}, "
        f"visits_conducted={stats['site_visits_conducted']}, "
        f"bookings_weekday={stats['bookings_weekday']}, "
        f"bookings_weekend={stats['bookings_weekend']}, "
        f"owners_with_activity={sum(1 for r in owner_rows if r['leads_generated'] or r['site_visits_scheduled'] or r['site_visits_conducted'] or r['bookings_total'])}")

    env = cls_watchdog.load_env()
    bot_token = env.get("TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN", "")
    chat_id = env.get("TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID", "")

    sent = False
    if not bot_token or not chat_id:
        log("TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN or TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID missing from .env — "
            "trying Brevo fallback directly.", "WARNING")
    else:
        sent = cls_watchdog.send_telegram(bot_token, chat_id, message)
        if not sent:
            log("Telegram send failed — attempting Brevo email fallback.", "WARNING")

    if not sent:
        sent = cls_watchdog.send_brevo_alert(env, message)

    summary = f"week {week_start.isoformat()}-{week_end.isoformat()}, delivered via {'Telegram' if bot_token and chat_id else 'Brevo'}" \
        if sent else f"week {week_start.isoformat()}-{week_end.isoformat()} computed, but delivery FAILED (Telegram and Brevo both failed)"
    cls_db.write_job_result("Monday Weekly Report", sent, summary)

    log("CLS MONDAY WEEKLY REPORT — END")
    log("=" * 55)
    return sent


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# SELF-TEST MODE
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def selftest():
    """
    Sends a fixed test message via the same send path — no DB query.
    Same self-test shape as cls_weekend_visits_report.py --selftest.
    """
    print("=" * 55)
    print(" CLS MONDAY WEEKLY REPORT — SELF TEST")
    print("=" * 55)

    env = cls_watchdog.load_env()
    bot_token = env.get("TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN", "")
    chat_id = env.get("TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID", "")
    msg = (
        "✅ <b>CLS Monday Weekly Report — Connection Test</b>\n"
        "If you see this, the Monday weekly report can reach you.\n"
        f"Time: {datetime.now().strftime('%d %b %Y, %I:%M %p')}"
    )

    if not bot_token or not chat_id:
        print("[FAIL] TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN or TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID not found in .env")
    else:
        print(f"[OK]   TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN found (last 6 chars: ...{bot_token[-6:]})")
        print(f"[OK]   TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID: {chat_id}")
        print()
        print("Sending test message to Telegram...")
        success = cls_watchdog.send_telegram(bot_token, chat_id, msg)
        if success:
            print("[OK]   Test message delivered. Check your Telegram.")
        else:
            print("[FAIL] Telegram delivery failed. Trying Brevo fallback...")
            ok = cls_watchdog.send_brevo_alert(env, msg)
            if ok:
                print("[OK]   Brevo fallback email sent. Check sales1@asianbuild.in inbox.")
            else:
                print("[FAIL] Brevo fallback also failed. Check .env credentials and logs.")

    print()
    print("Self-test complete.")
    print("=" * 55)


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# ENTRY POINT
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

if __name__ == "__main__":
    if "--selftest" in sys.argv:
        selftest()
    else:
        main()

```

<!-- modified: 15d ago | last git commit: 2026-08-17 | in a .bat wrapper: yes | imported elsewhere: no -->
```python
"""
=============================================================
cls_weekend_visits_report.py  —  CLS Weekend Site Visits Report
=============================================================
Version : 1.0
Author  : Built for Asian Properties / Srikanth

CHANGELOG
---------
v1.0 (2026-08-17) — Initial version. Replaces Srikanth's manual Friday
  headcount ask ("how many site visits this weekend?") with an automated
  Telegram report. Ops-only script, outside the Job A-D pipeline naming
  (not "Job E" in job_results.txt — see write_job_result() call below) —
  it doesn't participate in the A-B-C-D flag-gated hand-off chain, it
  just reads cls_db.get_weekend_site_visits() (cls_db.py v2.59) on its
  own Friday-afternoon Task Scheduler trigger. No Sell.do-side check —
  Sell.do was fully retired 2026-08-15 (see cls_db.py v2.57's
  changelog), so site_visits is the sole, authoritative source now.

WHAT THIS SCRIPT DOES
----------------------
Every Friday afternoon (Task Scheduler, see run_cls_weekend_visits_
report.bat), pulls every 'scheduled' site visit falling on the coming
Saturday or Sunday, groups it by salesperson, and sends Srikanth a
Telegram message (HTML parse_mode, same as cls_watchdog.py) with a
per-salesperson breakdown. Falls back to a Brevo email if Telegram is
unavailable — same primary/fallback pattern cls_watchdog.py's run()
uses, reusing its load_env()/send_telegram()/send_brevo_alert() rather
than duplicating that logic.

USAGE
-----
  python cls_weekend_visits_report.py             # normal run
  python cls_weekend_visits_report.py --selftest  # sends a fixed test
                                                    # message, no DB query
"""

import os
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from itertools import groupby

BASE_DIR = r"D:\CLS"
sys.path.insert(0, BASE_DIR)
import cls_db
import cls_watchdog   # reuse load_env()/send_telegram()/send_brevo_alert() —
                       # its own run logic lives behind __main__, so importing
                       # it here has no side effects.

LOG_FILE = os.path.join(BASE_DIR, "cls_weekend_visits_log.txt")

# pythonw.exe has no console — sys.stdout is None. Guard before reconfiguring.
if sys.stdout is not None:
    sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# LOGGING
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def log(message, level="INFO"):
    ts = datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
    entry = f"[{ts}] [{level}] {message}"
    try:
        if sys.stdout is not None:
            print(entry)
    except Exception:
        pass
    try:
        os.makedirs(BASE_DIR, exist_ok=True)
        with open(LOG_FILE, "a", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
            f.write(entry + "\n")
    except Exception:
        pass


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# MESSAGE BUILDING
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def _weekend_dates():
    """
    Saturday/Sunday of the upcoming weekend — same 'stay put if today
    IS Saturday' rule as cls_db.get_weekend_site_visits()'s SQL
    ('weekday 6'), computed here in Python purely for display in the
    Telegram header. Python's date.weekday(): Monday=0 ... Saturday=5,
    Sunday=6 — days_ahead=0 when today is already Saturday.
    """
    today = datetime.now().date()
    days_ahead = (5 - today.weekday()) % 7
    saturday = today + timedelta(days=days_ahead)
    sunday = saturday + timedelta(days=1)
    return saturday, sunday


def _format_visit_time(scheduled_at):
    """Same 12-hour display convention as app.py's 'ampm' Jinja filter."""
    if not scheduled_at:
        return "—"
    for fmt in ("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"):
        try:
            dt = datetime.strptime(scheduled_at, fmt)
            return dt.strftime("%a, %I:%M %p")
        except ValueError:
            continue
    return scheduled_at


def build_message(visits):
    """
    Builds the HTML-formatted Telegram message. Returns a string.
    Zero-visits case still returns a real message — never skip sending
    silently, Srikanth should know the job ran even when there's nothing
    to report.
    """
    saturday, sunday = _weekend_dates()
    date_range = f"{saturday.strftime('%a, %b %d')} – {sunday.strftime('%a, %b %d')}"
    total = len(visits)

    if total == 0:
        return (
            f"📅 <b>Weekend Site Visits — {date_range}</b>\n"
            f"No site visits scheduled for this weekend."
        )

    lines = [
        f"📅 <b>Weekend Site Visits — {date_range}</b>",
        f"Total: <b>{total}</b> visit(s) scheduled",
    ]
    for owner, owner_visits in groupby(visits, key=lambda v: v["lead_owner"] or "Unassigned"):
        owner_visits = list(owner_visits)
        lines.append(f"\n👤 <b>{owner}</b> ({len(owner_visits)})")
        for v in owner_visits:
            when = _format_visit_time(v["scheduled_at"])
            phone = v["phone_raw"] or "—"
            project = v["project"] or "—"
            lines.append(f"• {v['full_name']} — {phone} — {project} — {when}")

    return "\n".join(lines)


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# MAIN
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def main():
    log("=" * 55)
    log("CLS WEEKEND SITE VISITS REPORT — START")
    log("=" * 55)

    visits = cls_db.get_weekend_site_visits()
    message = build_message(visits)
    log(f"{len(visits)} site visit(s) found for the upcoming weekend.")

    env = cls_watchdog.load_env()
    bot_token = env.get("TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN", "")
    chat_id = env.get("TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID", "")

    sent = False
    if not bot_token or not chat_id:
        log("TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN or TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID missing from .env — "
            "trying Brevo fallback directly.", "WARNING")
    else:
        sent = cls_watchdog.send_telegram(bot_token, chat_id, message)
        if not sent:
            log("Telegram send failed — attempting Brevo email fallback.", "WARNING")

    if not sent:
        sent = cls_watchdog.send_brevo_alert(env, message)

    summary = f"{len(visits)} visit(s), delivered via {'Telegram' if bot_token and chat_id else 'Brevo'}" \
        if sent else f"{len(visits)} visit(s) found, but delivery FAILED (Telegram and Brevo both failed)"
    cls_db.write_job_result("Weekend Site Visits Report", sent, summary)

    log("CLS WEEKEND SITE VISITS REPORT — END")
    log("=" * 55)
    return sent


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# SELF-TEST MODE
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def selftest():
    """
    Sends a fixed test message via the same send path — no DB query.
    Same self-test shape as cls_watchdog.py --selftest.
    """
    print("=" * 55)
    print(" CLS WEEKEND SITE VISITS REPORT — SELF TEST")
    print("=" * 55)

    env = cls_watchdog.load_env()
    bot_token = env.get("TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN", "")
    chat_id = env.get("TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID", "")
    msg = (
        "✅ <b>CLS Weekend Site Visits Report — Connection Test</b>\n"
        "If you see this, the weekend visits report can reach you.\n"
        f"Time: {datetime.now().strftime('%d %b %Y, %I:%M %p')}"
    )

    if not bot_token or not chat_id:
        print("[FAIL] TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN or TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID not found in .env")
    else:
        print(f"[OK]   TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN found (last 6 chars: ...{bot_token[-6:]})")
        print(f"[OK]   TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID: {chat_id}")
        print()
        print("Sending test message to Telegram...")
        success = cls_watchdog.send_telegram(bot_token, chat_id, msg)
        if success:
            print("[OK]   Test message delivered. Check your Telegram.")
        else:
            print("[FAIL] Telegram delivery failed. Trying Brevo fallback...")
            ok = cls_watchdog.send_brevo_alert(env, msg)
            if ok:
                print("[OK]   Brevo fallback email sent. Check sales1@asianbuild.in inbox.")
            else:
                print("[FAIL] Brevo fallback also failed. Check .env credentials and logs.")

    print()
    print("Self-test complete.")
    print("=" * 55)


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# ENTRY POINT
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

if __name__ == "__main__":
    if "--selftest" in sys.argv:
        selftest()
    else:
        main()
```

```python
"""
=============================================================
 cls_whatsapp_encoding_check.py  —  v1.0
=============================================================
PURPOSE
-------
One-off, READ-ONLY diagnostic for the WhatsApp emoji-corruption
complaint (2026-08-27). Does two things:

  1. Prints the SQLite database's own text encoding (PRAGMA encoding).
     If this is anything other than UTF-8, that IS the root cause —
     SQLite's UTF-16 storage modes are known to mishandle 4-byte
     (astral-plane) UTF-8 characters like most emoji.

  2. Scans whatsapp_templates and whatsapp_reminder_templates for any
     message_body already containing U+FFFD (the "�" replacement
     character) — i.e. already-corrupted rows, listed by project name
     so you know exactly which templates need re-pasting from a clean
     source (chat, not Notepad/Word/WhatsApp-app-draft).

Makes NO writes. Safe to run any time, including while the CRM app or
scheduled jobs are running (WAL mode allows concurrent reads).

USAGE
-----
  python cls_whatsapp_encoding_check.py            (checks CLS1.db)
  python cls_whatsapp_encoding_check.py CLS2.db     (checks another DB)

CHANGELOG
---------
v1.0 (2026-08-27) — initial version.
=============================================================
"""

import os
import sys
import sqlite3

BASE_DIR = r"D:\CLS"
DB_NAME = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else os.environ.get("CLS_DB_PATH", "CLS1.db")
DB_FILE = DB_NAME if os.path.isabs(DB_NAME) else os.path.join(BASE_DIR, DB_NAME)

REPLACEMENT_CHAR = "\ufffd"


def _p(msg=""):
    # Guard against pythonw.exe / non-console contexts setting stdout=None
    try:
        print(msg)
    except Exception:
        pass


def scan_table(conn, table, project_col="project", body_col="message_body"):
    try:
        rows = conn.execute(f"SELECT {project_col}, {body_col} FROM {table}").fetchall()
    except sqlite3.OperationalError as e:
        _p(f"  [SKIP] {table}: {e}")
        return []

    hits = []
    for project, body in rows:
        if body and REPLACEMENT_CHAR in body:
            count = body.count(REPLACEMENT_CHAR)
            idx = body.find(REPLACEMENT_CHAR)
            start = max(0, idx - 15)
            end = min(len(body), idx + 15)
            snippet = body[start:end].replace("\n", " ")
            hits.append((project, count, snippet))
    return hits


def main():
    if not os.path.exists(DB_FILE):
        _p(f"[FAIL] Database not found at {DB_FILE}")
        return

    conn = sqlite3.connect(DB_FILE, timeout=30)

    _p("=" * 65)
    _p(" CLS WHATSAPP TEMPLATE ENCODING CHECK (read-only)")
    _p(f" DB: {DB_FILE}")
    _p("=" * 65)

    # ── 1. Database-level text encoding ──
    encoding = conn.execute("PRAGMA encoding;").fetchone()[0]
    _p(f"\n[DB ENCODING] PRAGMA encoding = {encoding}")
    if encoding.lower() != "utf-8":
        _p("  [!!] NOT UTF-8. This is very likely the root cause —")
        _p("       SQLite UTF-16 storage modes are known to corrupt")
        _p("       4-byte (astral-plane) UTF-8 characters, which is")
        _p("       exactly the class of character (most emoji) that's")
        _p("       breaking. This cannot be fixed by re-pasting alone —")
        _p("       flag this back and we'll scope a proper fix.")
    else:
        _p("  [OK] UTF-8 — database storage layer is not the cause.")
        _p("       Corruption is happening at INSERT time (before the")
        _p("       text reaches SQLite) — i.e. wherever the template")
        _p("       text is typed/pasted/imported from.")

    # ── 2. Scan both template tables for already-corrupted rows ──
    _p("\n[SCAN] whatsapp_templates (welcome-message templates)")
    hits1 = scan_table(conn, "whatsapp_templates")
    if hits1:
        for project, count, snippet in hits1:
            _p(f"  [CORRUPT] project='{project}'  {count} replacement char(s)")
            _p(f"            ...{snippet}...")
    else:
        _p("  [OK] No U+FFFD found in any row.")

    _p("\n[SCAN] whatsapp_reminder_templates (site-visit reminder templates)")
    hits2 = scan_table(conn, "whatsapp_reminder_templates")
    if hits2:
        for project, count, snippet in hits2:
            _p(f"  [CORRUPT] project='{project}'  {count} replacement char(s)")
            _p(f"            ...{snippet}...")
    else:
        _p("  [OK] No U+FFFD found in any row.")

    conn.close()

    _p("\n" + "-" * 65)
    total = len(hits1) + len(hits2)
    if total:
        _p(f"[SUMMARY] {total} template(s) need re-pasting from a clean source.")
    else:
        _p("[SUMMARY] No corrupted templates found in the DB right now.")
        _p("          If Naishka's template still showed '�' before you")
        _p("          re-pasted it, that row is what was corrupted — this")
        _p("          scan only sees what's in the DB at the moment you run it.")
    _p("=" * 65)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```
